closing.lede: Your advisor arranges the flights, the rooms and the visa — the trip, handled.

seo.title: Nairobi & the Mara — TripAgent
seo.description: Nairobi & the Mara, in hand: where to stay, what to do, where to eat and where the night goes — the addresses worth knowing.

hero.name: Nairobi & the Mara
hero.tagline: Kenya's vivid capital and the legendary Mara plains.

ourTake.lede: Nairobi is a working city, not a sight to linger over — treat it as the hinge between arrival and the Mara, one or two nights to reset. The move that separates a good trip from an ordinary one is basing inside a private conservancy bordering the reserve rather than the main reserve itself, where you trade shared roads and vehicle jams for off-road driving, night drives and walking. Fly to camp; the road transfer eats a day you don't have.
ourTake.comeIf: You want the definitive African safari — the Migration, private conservancies and camps where the wild comes to your veranda.
ourTake.skipIf: You need city polish and predictability; the Mara is about early mornings, dust and the untamed, not urban comforts.

firstLook.heroCaption: kenya destination

grid.caption: Modern pool villa with palms and umbrella
purple allium blooms in soft focus

whenToGo.blurb: July to October for the Great Migration river crossings, January to February for calving and clear skies. Avoid the long rains of April and May.
whenToGo.bestMonths: Jan, Feb, Aug, Sep, Nov and Dec

guide.lede: Where to stay, what to do, where to eat, and where the night goes — grouped by price, every address earned by a name worth trusting.

note.label: On credentials
note.text: Michelin’s inspectors don’t yet come to Nairobi & the Mara. So we don’t pretend a star — we credential its tables the way we’d want to be told: World’s 50 Best, Condé Nast Traveller, and the houses we would send our own family to.

items.name: Angama Mara
items.area: Maasai Mara — Oloololo Escarpment, above the Mara Triangle
credentials: Condé Nast Traveler Readers' Choice Awards — No. 1 Resort in Africa
items.description: Two intimate camps of glass-fronted tented suites suspended high on the escarpment, with the whole Mara falling away below — arguably the most cinematic view in Africa.

items.name: Mara Plains Camp
credentials: Relais & Châteaux (member since 2014 — Kenya's only Relais & Châteaux)
items.description: Great Plains Conservation's jewel — seven raised tented suites of leather, brass and old-safari romance on the Ntiakitiak River, in a big-cat conservancy off-limits to the crowds.

items.name: Bateleur Camp, &Beyond
items.area: Maasai Mara — Kichwa Tembo concession, western Mara
credentials: Condé Nast Traveler Readers' Choice Awards
items.description: 1920s Happy-Valley glamour reborn — swagged canvas, campaign furniture and butler service in a private forest concession beneath the Oloololo Escarpment.

items.name: Cottar's 1920s Camp
items.area: Maasai Mara — Olderkesi Private Conservancy (south-east, bordering the reserve)
credentials: Relais & Châteaux (the only Relais & Châteaux camp bordering the Maasai Mara reserve)
items.description: A fifth-generation family safari and a living time capsule — Persian rugs, steamer trunks and a gramophone that still plays, on its own private conservancy away from every crowd.

items.name: Giraffe Manor
credentials: Condé Nast Traveler Readers' Choice Awards — Top Hotels in Africa
items.description: Nairobi's most photographed address — a 1930s ivy-clad manor where the resident Rothschild's giraffes lean their heads through the breakfast windows.

items.name: Sanctuary Olonana
items.area: Maasai Mara — private stretch of the Mara River, within the reserve
credentials: Condé Nast Traveler Readers' Choice Awards
items.description: Abercrombie & Kent's riverside lodge — fourteen glass-walled suites over the Mara River, where hippos are the soundtrack and the crossings are minutes away.

items.name: Hemingways Nairobi
credentials: Small Luxury Hotels of the World
items.description: A crisp, colonnaded white manor in leafy Karen — 45 suites, a butler to each, and the calmest, most polished city base in Nairobi.

items.name: Sala's Camp
items.area: Maasai Mara — southern reserve, near the Sand and Keekorok rivers
credentials: Condé Nast Traveler Readers' Choice Awards
items.description: The Safari Collection's remote southern camp — first light on the Migration as it enters Kenya, and a fire-lit intimacy far from the day-trippers.

items.name: Fairmont The Norfolk
items.description: Kenya's original grand hotel, opened Christmas Day 1904 — Tudor gables, the storied Lord Delamere Terrace, and the city that grew up around it.

items.name: Masai Mara Big Five Game Drives
items.description: The Mara is the beating heart of a Kenya safari — open golden savannah studded with acacia and the highest density of big cats anywhere in Africa, where a single morning drive can deliver lion, leopard, elephant, buffalo and, with luck, black rhino. Fly in by light aircraft from Nairobi (about 45 minutes) to a maison-standard tented camp, and your private guide and tracker build the day around the sightings while you never share a vehicle.

items.name: The Great Migration & Mara River Crossings
credentials: Seven Natural Wonders of Africa — the Serengeti–Mara Migration
items.description: From roughly July to October, more than a million wildebeest and zebra pour up from the Serengeti and hurl themselves across the crocodile-filled Mara River in one of the planet's last great wildlife spectacles — chaos, dust and drama at the water's edge. Timing is everything and the finest camps sell out a year ahead, so this is the trip your advisor pins the whole itinerary around.

items.name: Hot-Air Balloon Safari at Dawn over the Mara
items.description: Lift off in the pre-dawn dark and drift in silence a few hundred feet above the plains as the sun comes up and the herds move below you — the single most romantic hour on any African safari, ending with a champagne bush breakfast laid out on white linen in the grass. A bucket-list morning that grandparents and honeymooners remember for the rest of their lives.

items.name: Angama Mara & the Escarpment Camps
items.description: Perched on the rim of the Great Rift Valley with glass-walled tented suites suspended 300 metres above the plains, Angama Mara has the most cinematic view in the Mara — the very ridge where the 'Out of Africa' picnic was filmed. This is the ultra-luxury tier of tented camp — private butlers, veg and Jain menus handled with care, and a swing seat over the endless savannah.

items.name: Mara North Conservancy
items.description: A vast private wilderness bordering the reserve where only a handful of camps share tens of thousands of acres, so a lion sighting is yours alone rather than ringed by twenty vans. Conservancy rules unlock off-road driving right up to the animals, night drives after leopard and aardvark, and guided walking — none of which the main reserve allows.

items.name: Olare Motorogi Conservancy
items.description: 35,000 acres of prime northern Mara with one of the densest lion populations in all of Africa and a strict low-vehicle limit, so exclusivity is written into the model — this is where Richard Branson's Mahali Mzuri sits. For a family that wants the game of the Mara without the crowds, this is the connoisseur's choice.

items.name: Mara Naboisho Conservancy
items.description: One of the largest community-owned conservancies in Africa at roughly 50,000 acres, with rolling hills, leopard-rich thickets and open valleys where cheetah coalitions hunt — and a genuine partnership that puts tourism money directly into Maasai landowners' hands. The walking safaris and night drives here are among the best in Kenya.

items.name: Walking Safari with a Maasai Guide
items.description: Step out of the vehicle and cross the savannah on foot with an armed ranger and a Maasai naturalist, learning to read tracks, dung and birdsong at the pace the bush was meant to be seen — a quiet, intimate counterpoint to the game drive. Only the private conservancies permit it, which is part of why the discerning traveller pays for them.

items.name: Sundowners on the Plains
items.description: The safari day closes with a ritual — your guide parks on a rise as the light turns molten, unpacks a bar from the back of the Land Cruiser, and you toast the day with the whole Mara glowing gold to the horizon. It costs nothing extra and it is, for many, the memory that outlasts the animals.

items.name: A Maasai Village Visit
items.description: A respectful, camp-arranged visit to a manyatta lets you meet the Maasai on their own terms — the jumping dance, fire-making, beadwork and a frank conversation about pastoral life alongside the wildlife. Choose one your camp partners with directly so the money reaches the community rather than a staged roadside show.

items.name: Photographic Safari with a Specialist Guide
items.description: Book a dedicated photographic vehicle — beanbags, a low open-sided rig, a guide who thinks in light and angles and will sit for an hour waiting for the leopard to yawn. For serious hobbyists and multi-gen families with a keen teenager behind the lens, it turns a game drive into a masterclass.

items.name: Nairobi National Park
items.description: The only national park in the world set inside a capital city — lions, giraffe, rhino and buffalo grazing against a backdrop of skyscrapers, minutes from your hotel. A perfect half-day on arrival or before the flight home, and a gentle first taste of the safari for children and grandparents (adult entry around USD 43).

items.name: Sheldrick Wildlife Trust Elephant Orphanage
items.description: The world's most famous orphan-elephant nursery, where rescued calves — many orphaned by poaching or drought — tumble through the mud and take their milk bottles at the one-hour public visit each day (11am, by advance booking only). Deeply moving, endlessly delightful for children, and a chance to foster a calf your family follows for years.

items.name: The Giraffe Centre (AFEW)
items.description: Set up in 1979 by the African Fund for Endangered Wildlife to save the endangered Rothschild's giraffe, this is where you hand-feed the giants from a raised wooden platform, eye to eye. Open daily 9am–5pm, minutes from the Sheldrick Trust — the two make a joyful, easy morning for all ages.

items.name: Breakfast with Giraffes at Giraffe Manor
items.description: The 1930s ivy-clad manor of the Safari Collection, where a resident herd of Rothschild's giraffes pokes its head through the dining-room windows at breakfast for a slice of toast — the most photographed hotel moment in Africa. The twelve rooms book many months ahead and the breakfast is for staying guests only, so it needs planning through your advisor.

items.name: Karen Blixen Museum ('Out of Africa')
items.description: The colonial farmhouse at the foot of the Ngong Hills where the Danish author of 'Out of Africa' lived from 1917, preserved with her furniture and the coffee plantation grounds — the film won seven Oscars and made this hill country legend. A gentle, literary hour open daily, best paired with the Giraffe Centre next door.

items.name: Nairobi National Museum & Snake Park
items.description: The flagship of the National Museums of Kenya — the human-origins hall with fossils from the Rift Valley, superb bird and ethnography galleries, and an adjacent snake park and botanical garden. Two or three cultured hours that give real context before you head to the bush.

items.name: Bomas of Kenya
items.description: A living cultural village recreating the homesteads of Kenya's major communities, with a large auditorium staging spirited traditional song and dance from across the country every afternoon. A colourful, family-friendly window on the cultures behind the wildlife.

items.name: Kazuri Beads Women's Cooperative
items.description: A ceramics workshop founded to employ single mothers, where you watch women hand-roll and glaze the clay beads and pottery sold worldwide, then buy directly from the floor — higher quality and a better story than the markets. A five-minute drive from the Giraffe Centre and a meaningful gift stop.

items.name: Kiambethu Tea Farm
items.description: A working tea estate in the cool green highlands above Nairobi, in the same family since 1910, where a guided walk explains the leaf, a stroll through indigenous forest may turn up colobus monkeys, and lunch is served on the lawn with valley views. A civilised, restful day trip that balances the adrenaline of the safari.

items.name: Ngong Hills Hike
items.description: The knuckled ridge that gives 'Out of Africa' its silhouette — a breezy walk over seven green peaks past a line of wind turbines, with the Rift Valley falling away on one side and the Nairobi skyline on the other. A bracing morning's exercise, best done with a guide, and a fine leg-stretch before or after the bush.

items.name: The Carnivore Restaurant
items.description: A Nairobi institution since 1980, this open-air 'nyama choma' feast roasts endless skewers of meat over a vast charcoal pit and carves them at your table until you lower the paper flag to surrender. A boisterous, only-in-Kenya dinner — and the kitchen will lay on a generous vegetarian spread for those who ask ahead.

items.name: The Maasai Market
items.description: The roving open-air craft market — beadwork, soapstone, wood carvings, kikoi cloth and kanga — that pitches at a different Nairobi location each day of the week (Village Market, the Junction, and more). Go with your guide, haggle gently, and take home the colour of Kenya.

items.name: Nairobi Railway Museum
items.description: The story of the 'Lunatic Line' — the railway the British drove from Mombasa to Lake Victoria, and the man-eating lions of Tsavo that stalked its builders — told through vintage locomotives and carriages you can climb aboard. Open daily 8am–5pm; a quiet, atmospheric hour for anyone curious about how modern Kenya was stitched together.

items.name: Amboseli National Park — Elephants beneath Kilimanjaro
items.description: The classic postcard of Africa: great herds of elephant crossing the dust with the snows of Kilimanjaro floating above them — Amboseli's flat, open floor gives the finest elephant viewing and the most famous mountain backdrop in Kenya. An easy light-aircraft hop and a natural pairing with the Mara for a two-park safari.

items.name: Lake Nakuru National Park — Flamingos & Rhinos
credentials: UNESCO World Heritage Site — Kenya Lake System in the Great Rift Valley
items.description: A shimmering soda lake famous for its pink drifts of flamingo and, more reliably now, one of Kenya's best places to see both black and white rhino, plus tree-climbing lions and Rothschild's giraffe. Part of the UNESCO-listed Kenya Lake System, and an easy addition to a Rift Valley loop.

items.name: Lake Bogoria & Lake Elementaita
credentials: UNESCO World Heritage Site — Kenya Lake System in the Great Rift Valley
items.description: Bogoria's steaming hot springs and geysers draw vast congregations of lesser flamingo, while quieter Elementaita completes the trio of alkaline lakes that hold up to four million birds between them. Together with Nakuru they form the UNESCO Kenya Lake System — a birder's and geologist's dream a couple of hours from Naivasha.

items.name: Lake Naivasha Boat Safari
items.description: A freshwater Rift Valley lake where a small boat glides you among hippo pods and past fish eagles snatching prey from the surface — gentle, scenic and a lovely change of tempo from the game drive. The lakeshore lodges make a relaxed base for exploring Hell's Gate and Crescent Island next door.

items.name: Crescent Island Walking Safari
items.description: A private sanctuary with no predators, so you can walk freely on foot among giraffe, zebra, eland, waterbuck and wildebeest — a rare, safe, unhurried way to be at eye level with plains game. Reached by a short boat ride across Naivasha and perfect for children old enough to walk a few kilometres.

items.name: Hell's Gate National Park by Bike
items.description: One of the very few Kenyan parks you can explore on a bicycle or on foot, cycling among zebra and giraffe between towering red cliffs and gorges — the landscape that inspired 'The Lion King'. An active, exhilarating half-day for families with teenagers who need to burn energy.

items.name: Samburu National Reserve — the Northern Specials
items.description: A rugged, arid reserve on the Ewaso Ng'iro river where you find species seen almost nowhere else on a Kenya safari — Grevy's zebra, reticulated giraffe, the long-necked gerenuk and beisa oryx — alongside big cats and elephant. The starkly beautiful, less-trodden north for travellers who have already done the Mara.

items.name: Ol Pejeta Conservancy — the Last Northern White Rhinos
items.description: The 360-square-kilometre conservancy that guards Najin and Fatu, the last two northern white rhinos on Earth, under armed round-the-clock protection — a chance to stand with a species at the very edge of existence. Also East Africa's largest black-rhino sanctuary and a genuinely purpose-driven place to bring children.

items.name: Sweetwaters Chimpanzee Sanctuary
items.description: The only place in Kenya to see chimpanzees — a Jane Goodall Institute sanctuary within Ol Pejeta that gives lifelong refuge to apes rescued from the illegal trade across Central and West Africa. A moving, educational stop that pairs naturally with the rhino experience.

items.name: Lewa Wildlife Conservancy
credentials: UNESCO World Heritage Site — extension of Mount Kenya National Park / Natural Forest
items.description: A pioneering private conservancy that holds a significant share of Kenya's rhino and, with the neighbouring Ngare Ndare forest, forms an official extension of the Mount Kenya UNESCO World Heritage Site. Horseback safaris, superb rhino viewing and a conservation model the world studies — the thinking traveller's safari.

items.name: Laikipia Plateau Private Ranches
items.description: A high, wild plateau of vast private conservancies and family-run ranches where the safari turns creative — horseback and camel treks, mountain-biking, fly-camping and night drives that the national parks never allow. Sparse, exclusive and endlessly varied, it is where repeat Kenya travellers go for something new.

items.name: Mount Kenya National Park
credentials: UNESCO World Heritage Site — Mount Kenya National Park / Natural Forest
items.description: Africa's second-highest peak, its glacier-hung summit and afro-alpine moorland rising straight from the equator — you can trek the scenic Chogoria or Sirimon routes to the trekker's summit of Point Lenana over several days. A UNESCO World Heritage Site and a serious highland adventure to bolt onto a classic safari.

items.name: Tsavo East & Tsavo West — the Red Elephants
items.description: Kenya's largest wilderness — bigger than some countries — where elephants dust themselves in the brick-red iron soil and glow terracotta, and Mzima Springs runs crystal-clear among hippo and crocodile. Raw, vast and uncrowded, and the natural bridge between a Nairobi safari and the Indian Ocean coast.

items.name: Diani Beach — Bush & Beach
items.description: Powder-white sand and warm turquoise water on the palm-fringed south coast, the classic way to end a Kenya safari — swap the Land Cruiser for a dhow, a spa and a lounger. Just up from Tsavo, it makes the effortless bush-and-beach combination that Indian families love for the multi-generational reward at the end.

items.name: Watamu & the Marine National Parks
items.description: A quieter coral-coast alternative to Diani, with a protected marine park for snorkelling and diving over reefs, a turtle-watch programme, and the mangrove creeks of Mida — plus the atmospheric Gede ruins nearby. Bush-and-beach with a gentler, more natural rhythm.

items.name: Private Conservancy Night Game Drives
items.description: After dark, a red-filtered spotlight reveals a whole second Africa the daytime hides — hunting leopard, aardvark, bat-eared fox, genet and the eyes of a lion on the move. Available only on the private conservancies, it is one of the clearest reasons to pay for that exclusivity.

items.name: Conservation & Anti-Poaching Experiences
items.description: Many top camps let guests spend a morning with the people doing the work — tracking rhino on foot with the monitoring team, meeting the canine anti-poaching unit, or joining a research drive. A purposeful, behind-the-scenes half-day that turns a luxury holiday into something the whole family carries home.

items.name: Light-Aircraft Safari Transfers
items.description: The way discerning travellers move around Kenya — a scheduled or private Cessna from Nairobi's Wilson Airport hops you to a Mara or Amboseli airstrip in under an hour, over the Rift Valley and the herds, sparing hours of rough road. Book the private charter for total flexibility on timing and camps.

items.name: Governors' Camp & Little Governors'
items.description: The grande dame of Mara camps, sitting on a prime bend of the Mara River inside the reserve where the migration crosses right in front of the tents, run with old-world safari polish for generations. For travellers who want the classic reserve position and heritage rather than a conservancy, this is the benchmark.

items.name: Mahali Mzuri
items.description: Richard Branson's twelve-tent camp in the lion-rich Olare Motorogi conservancy — pod-like suites tumbling down a hillside above a wildlife corridor, all game drives, walks and night drives included, with a spa and impeccable service. The polished, design-forward end of the Mara for a couple or a family seeking privacy.

items.name: Chyulu Hills & the Kilimanjaro Foothills
items.description: The rolling green volcanic hills Hemingway called the 'Green Hills of Africa', where private wilderness camps offer horseback and walking safaris in the shadow of Kilimanjaro on Maasai-owned land. A serene, low-density extension for those who have seen the headline parks and want the road less travelled.

items.name: Talisman
items.description: Nairobi's most-loved restaurant — a rambling colonial house in Karen, oriental rugs and fireplaces, and an East-African-meets-global menu that has defined city dining for two decades.

items.name: INTI
items.description: Nikkei cooking — Japanese precision married to Peruvian fire — from a rooftop with the Nairobi skyline laid out below, and a Pisco Sour to match.

items.name: Cultiva
items.area: Naivasha (day trip from Nairobi / en route to the Rift)
items.description: A farm-to-table kitchen in a lakeside garden — much of the menu grown on the property, and one of Kenya's most talked-about dining rooms.

items.name: Lord Delamere Terrace
items.description: Breakfast, lunch or a sundowner on the terrace that has watched Nairobi go by since 1904 — the city's most storied place to sit and take it in.

items.name: The Carnivore
credentials: Ranked No. 47, World's Best 50 Restaurants (2003) — a Nairobi icon
items.description: The great Nairobi institution — an open-air 'beast of a feast' where skewers of roast meats are carved at your table until you lower the paper flag.

items.name: Nyama Mama
credentials: Notable Nairobi venue — Kenyan comfort food, widely recognised
items.description: A bright, playful 'modern African diner' reinventing Kenyan home cooking — ugali, nyama and coastal Swahili plates with colour and wit.

items.name: Bush sundowners & the campfire
credentials: The signature evening ritual of every Mara lodge
items.description: The Mara's true nightlife — a drink poured on a rise as the sun drops behind the escarpment, then dinner and stories around the fire under the biggest sky you'll ever see.

items.name: Lord Delamere Terrace & Bar
items.description: A sundowner on the 1904 terrace where every explorer, settler and safari-goer has raised a glass — the most historic drink in Kenya.

items.name: Giraffe Manor drawing room
items.description: An evening drink by the fire in the ivy-clad manor, giraffes wandering the lawn outside the leaded windows — a private, storybook nightcap.

items.name: INTI Rooftop
items.description: Nairobi's most stylish rooftop — Pisco Sours and Nikkei small plates over the city lights, from a bar team as serious as the kitchen.

items.title: River crossing from a Mara North conservancy camp
items.description: Watching wildebeest brave the crocodile-heavy Mara River from a private-conservancy vehicle keeps you clear of the reserve's crossing-point crowds.

items.title: Dawn balloon flight over the plains
items.description: A quiet hour above the herds at first light, landing to a bush breakfast laid out on the grass.

items.title: Walking safari with a Maasai guide
items.description: On foot with a spotter you read tracks and small signs the vehicle rushes past — only possible on private land.

items.title: Giraffe Manor breakfast in Nairobi
items.description: Rothschild's giraffes leaning through the windows at breakfast is genuinely singular, and worth the early booking it demands.

plan.heading: 6 days in Nairobi & the Mara, done well
plan.lede: A day-by-day shape for the trip — the pace we would set. Your advisor books the flights and the rooms; the days are yours.

slots.label: Morning
slots.text: Settle into Hemingways Nairobi in Karen, then a quiet late breakfast on the terrace.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.text: Private visit to the Giraffe Centre and the David Sheldrick elephant orphanage, arranged for the calm hour before the crowds.

slots.label: Evening
slots.text: Dinner at Talisman in Karen, unhurried, with a table booked in the garden room.

slots.label: Morning
slots.text: Karen Blixen's farmhouse and the Ngong foothills, then coffee at a working estate above the city.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.text: The Nairobi National Museum with a curator, followed by an hour among the beadwork at Kazuri.

slots.label: Evening
slots.text: Chef's table dinner at Cultiva or a quiet evening at the hotel before the early flight.

slots.label: Morning
slots.text: Light-aircraft transfer from Wilson to an airstrip in the Mara Triangle, met by your guide.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.text: Settle into Angama Mara on the escarpment, then an unhurried first game drive as the plains fill.

slots.label: Evening
slots.text: Sundowners at the edge of the Rift, dinner brought to the deck under the stars.

slots.label: Morning
slots.text: Dawn drive in the private Mara Triangle, following the guide's read of the light and the herds.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.text: Rest through the heat, lunch overlooking the plains, then a slow afternoon on the river.

slots.label: Evening
slots.text: Bush dinner laid out by the camp, lanterns and a fire, guides telling the day back to you.

slots.label: Morning
slots.text: Full-day drive with a packed breakfast, tracking the Mara River crossings if the season allows.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.text: A quiet lunch in the shade, then time to simply watch — no schedule, just the plains.

slots.label: Evening
slots.text: Private dinner on the Out of Africa kopje, the whole valley below you.

slots.label: Morning
slots.text: A final dawn drive, unhurried, then breakfast as the balloons lift over the plains.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.text: Light-aircraft transfer back to Nairobi, day room held at Hemingways to freshen up.

slots.label: Evening
slots.text: Early supper and a discreet transfer to Jomo Kenyatta for the night flight home.

cta.label: Have your advisor arrange the stay

items.name: Karen
items.description: Leafy, colonial-era estates near the giraffe centre and Karen Blixen house — calm, green, best for a soft first night.

items.name: Mara North Conservancy
items.description: Private land on the reserve's edge; low vehicle density and off-road access, for travellers who want exclusivity over price.

items.name: Gigiri
items.description: The diplomatic quarter near the UN — secure, quiet and convenient to the airport for a functional stopover.

events.name: Great Wildebeest Migration river crossings
events.note: Peak crossing season in the Mara; the exact days are unpredictable, so allow several nights and book camps 12-18 months ahead.

events.name: WRC Safari Rally Kenya
events.note: The historic World Rally round runs on the rough tracks around Lake Naivasha, a couple of hours from Nairobi.

events.name: Lamu Cultural Festival
events.note: Dhow races, poetry and Swahili weddings on the coastal island — a natural add-on if you extend beyond the safari.

onGround.heading: On the ground

rows.label: Arriving
rows.value: Land at Nairobi's Jomo Kenyatta International (NBO), overnight at Hemingways or Giraffe Manor, then fly into the Mara by light aircraft from Wilson Airport to a private airstrip where your camp's ranger meets you.

rows.label: Getting around
rows.value: In the Mara you move by open 4x4 with a dedicated guide and tracker; in Nairobi a private chauffeur is standard given traffic and distance.

rows.label: Connectivity
rows.value: Safaricom eSIM covers Nairobi and most Mara camps well; deep-bush conservancies rely on camp Wi-Fi and Starlink, so treat true off-grid stretches as intentional.

rows.label: Money
rows.value: Kenyan shilling (KES); US dollars are widely accepted for park fees and camps, cards work in Nairobi, and guides/camp staff appreciate discreet USD tips.

onGround.note: Choose a private conservancy (Mara North, Naboisho, Olare Motorogi) over the reserve itself for exclusivity, night drives and off-road access; July falls in the Great Migration window, and evenings at altitude are cold, so pack a layer.

rows.label: Climate
rows.value: Dry season July-October is the reliable window: clear plains, thinned vegetation and the wildebeest river crossings; skip the long rains of April-May when tracks flood and camps thin out.

rows.label: Flights from India
rows.value: Kenya Airways flies Mumbai-Nairobi nonstop in about 6h30m; from Delhi and Bengaluru it is one stop via Mumbai or a Gulf hub (Emirates, Qatar) in J. Nairobi is the connection point for the light-aircraft hop into the Mara, so allow a comfortable overnight rather than a same-day tag-on to the bush camp.

rows.label: Health & safety
rows.value: Yellow fever certificate is required for onward Tanzania and often checked; malaria prophylaxis for the Mara, and routine vaccines current. Nairobi warrants city sense after dark; the private conservancies are secure. Drink bottled or filtered water.

rows.label: Dining, veg & Jain
rows.value: Vegetarian and Jain are well understood; the top Mara camps cater to both with notice, and Nairobi has real Indian cooking. Consider a night at Chowpaty or Haandi in Nairobi before flying into camp.

seo.title: New York — TripAgent
seo.description: New York, in hand: where to stay, what to do, where to eat and where the night goes — the addresses worth knowing.

hero.name: New York
hero.tagline: Ambition, art and appetite, all at once, all night.

ourTake.lede: New York is a city of neighbourhoods, not landmarks; pick a base with a good coffee and a good bar and let the blocks around it be the trip. Book the restaurant of the moment weeks ahead and see one great museum properly rather than three in a blur, the Met alone is a full, unhurried day. Skip Times Square beyond a single glance and give the time instead to the West Village, the High Line at dawn, and the outer-borough tables the guidebooks miss.
ourTake.comeIf: You want the full weight of a great world city — galleries, tables, theatre, and shopping in a single week.
ourTake.skipIf: You are after quiet, nature, or a slow pace; this city never fully exhales.

guide.lede: Where to stay, what to do, where to eat, and where the night goes — grouped by price, every address earned by a name worth trusting.

items.name: Aman New York
items.description: A hushed vertical sanctuary in the Crown Building — the city, finally, on silent.

items.name: The Mark Hotel
credentials: World's 50 Best Hotels 2025 (No. 43, only NYC entry)
items.description: The Upper East Side's most glamorous house — the only New York hotel on the world list.

items.name: The Carlyle, A Rosewood Hotel
items.description: Old-New-York grandeur with a cabaret in the basement — the city's most storied address.

items.name: Casa Cipriani New York
items.description: A members'-club hotel in a landmark ferry terminal — Italian glamour on the water's edge.

items.name: The Greenwich Hotel — Tribeca Penthouse
items.description: A one-of-a-kind Japanese-crafted penthouse above the Greenwich — the city's most private suite.

items.name: The Peninsula New York
items.description: A Beaux-Arts landmark on Fifth, with the group's famous precision and a rooftop bar.

items.name: Mandarin Oriental, New York
items.description: Park-and-skyline views from on high at Columbus Circle — the group's calm, precise flagship.

items.name: Four Seasons Hotel New York Downtown
items.description: The surest hands in Lower Manhattan — service you never have to think about.

items.name: The St. Regis New York
items.description: The house that invented the butler — Astor-era Beaux-Arts splendour off Fifth Avenue.

items.name: The Ritz-Carlton New York, Central Park
items.description: Park-facing tradition on Central Park South — grand, gracious, and reliably excellent.

items.name: Baccarat Hotel New York
items.description: Crystal-chandelier glamour opposite MoMA — a jewel-box of a hotel, and it knows it.

items.name: Park Hyatt New York
items.description: A calm, contemporary tower on Billionaires' Row — quiet luxury, beautifully run.

items.name: The Towers at Lotte New York Palace
items.description: A hotel-within-a-hotel in a Gilded-Age courtyard mansion — the exclusive Towers wing.

items.name: Crosby Street Hotel, Firmdale Hotels
items.description: Firmdale's English-country-house colour dropped into the heart of SoHo.

items.name: The Whitby Hotel, Firmdale Hotels
items.description: A joyful, art-filled Firmdale house a whisper from Fifth Avenue and Central Park.

items.name: The Lowell
items.description: A discreet townhouse hotel of wood fires and fresh flowers — old-money calm.

items.name: The Greenwich Hotel
items.description: Robert De Niro's Tribeca hideaway — a warm, worldly house with a lantern-lit pool.

items.name: The Fifth Avenue Hotel
items.description: A gilded mansion-and-tower debut — maximalist, romantic, the talk of NoMad.

items.name: Hotel Barrière Fouquet's New York
items.description: Parisian glamour on the Hudson side of Tribeca — the Champs-Élysées, restaged downtown.

items.name: Warren Street Hotel, Firmdale Hotels
items.description: Firmdale's downtown debut — the same fearless colour, now in Tribeca.

items.name: Trump International Hotel & Tower New York
items.description: Full Central Park frontage at Columbus Circle — big windows, big views.

items.name: Pendry Manhattan West
items.description: A sleek new-build in the Hudson Yards district — polished, contemporary, well-run.

items.name: Nine Orchard
items.description: A landmark 1912 bank turned design-led hotel — the coolest room downtown.

items.name: 1 Hotel Central Park
items.description: Nature-led calm steps from Central Park — reclaimed wood, living walls, easy comfort.

items.name: The Beekman, A Thompson Hotel
items.description: A breathtaking nine-storey Victorian atrium downtown — history with a modern pulse.

items.name: The Wall Street Hotel
items.description: A quietly elegant house in the old financial heart — a calm downtown residence.

items.name: The Mercer
items.description: The original SoHo loft hotel — spare, timeless, and endlessly cool.

items.name: The Bowery Hotel
items.description: A dimly-lit, velvet-and-candles downtown classic — romantic and a little bohemian.

items.name: The Ritz-Carlton New York, NoMad
items.description: A tall, contemporary Ritz-Carlton with a rooftop over the Empire State Building.

items.name: The Surrey, A Corinthia Hotel
items.description: A refined Upper East Side residence, newly reborn under Corinthia — quiet, gracious calm.

items.name: The Twenty Two New York
items.description: The London members'-club hotel's first New York address — buzzy and of-the-moment.

items.name: 1 Hotel Brooklyn Bridge
items.description: The best Manhattan-skyline view in the city — from the Brooklyn side of the river.

items.name: The New York EDITION
items.description: Understated elegance in a landmark clock tower over Madison Square Park.

items.name: The Ludlow Hotel
items.description: A relaxed, downtown-cool house on the Lower East Side — effortless and unpretentious.

items.name: Hotel Chelsea
items.description: The most legendary bohemian hotel in America — reborn, and steeped in its own myth.

items.name: Wythe Hotel
items.description: A converted Williamsburg factory with a rooftop bar and the skyline across the water.

items.name: Ace Hotel Brooklyn
items.description: A design-led, art-filled house in brownstone Brooklyn — relaxed and creative.

items.name: The Metropolitan Museum of Art
credentials: One of the world's great encyclopedic museums
Most-visited museum in the United States
items.description: Five thousand years of art in one building on Fifth Avenue — do the Temple of Dendur, the European paintings and the rooftop bar, then let the rest go; it's too big for one day.

items.name: The Museum of Modern Art (MoMA)
credentials: One of the world's foremost modern-art museums
items.description: Van Gogh's Starry Night, Monet's Water Lilies room, Warhol and Picasso — the modern canon in a light-filled building; go at opening or in the last two hours to dodge the crush.

items.name: The Solomon R. Guggenheim Museum
items.description: Frank Lloyd Wright's white spiral is the reason to come as much as the art — take the lift up and walk the ramp down past the Kandinskys.

items.name: The Frick Collection
items.description: A steel baron's Fifth Avenue mansion hung with Vermeer, Rembrandt and Bellini — reopened April 2025 after a $220m restoration that finally opened the family's upstairs rooms to the public; the most civilised hour of art in the city.

items.name: The Whitney Museum of American Art
items.description: Renzo Piano's museum of American art at the foot of the High Line — Hopper, O'Keeffe, Basquiat inside, and terraces that frame the Hudson and downtown skyline for free.

items.name: The Met Cloisters
items.description: The Met's medieval outpost, built from real French monastery cloisters on a bluff over the Hudson — the Unicorn Tapestries, herb gardens and river views make the subway ride uptown worth it. A quiet gem most visitors miss.

items.name: The Morgan Library & Museum
items.description: J.P. Morgan's private study and jewel-box library — Gutenberg Bibles, illuminated manuscripts and a domed rotunda in the financier's own home. Small, sumptuous, rarely crowded.

items.name: The American Museum of Natural History
items.description: Blue whale, dinosaur halls and the Rose planetarium plus the new Gilder science wing — the single best half-day in the city for children and multi-generational groups.

items.name: The Neue Galerie
items.description: A small mansion museum for German and Austrian art — home to Klimt's gold Woman in Gold — with Café Sabarsky downstairs for Viennese pastry. A refined pairing of art and Kaffeehaus.

items.name: The Noguchi Museum
items.description: Isamu Noguchi's own studio turned into a museum of stone sculpture around a still garden — a meditative escape a short hop across the river. Pair it with nearby Socrates Sculpture Park.

items.name: 9/11 Memorial & Museum
items.description: Two black reflecting pools in the tower footprints and a museum beneath ground zero — sobering and beautifully done; book the museum ahead and allow a quiet couple of hours.

items.name: Statue of Liberty & Ellis Island
items.description: The harbour crossing and the immigration halls are the real experience — book crown or pedestal access weeks ahead through your advisor, as they sell out; families can trace ancestors in the Ellis Island records.

items.name: Empire State Building
items.description: The 86th-floor open-air deck still delivers the classic New York view; the redone second-floor museum is genuinely good. Go at dusk to catch daylight and the lit city in one visit.

items.name: Top of the Rock, Rockefeller Center
items.description: The best skyline view precisely because it looks back at the Empire State and up Central Park — three open decks, no glass in your photos. The new 'Beam' rooftop experience is a fun add-on.

items.name: Summit One Vanderbilt
items.area: Midtown East / next to Grand Central
items.description: The most theatrical observation deck — mirrored rooms, glass-floor ledges over Madison Avenue and glass 'Ascent' lifts on the building's flank; part art installation, part view. Book a timed slot.

items.name: Edge at Hudson Yards
items.description: The Western Hemisphere's highest outdoor sky deck, with an angled glass floor and a lean-out corner over the West Side; adrenaline-seekers can add the 'City Climb' harnessed ascent up the building's exterior.

items.name: One World Observatory
items.description: Top of the tallest tower in the Western Hemisphere — a fast lift with a time-lapse of the city's rise, then harbour-to-Manhattan views. Best paired with the 9/11 Memorial below.

items.name: The Staten Island Ferry
items.description: The best free thing in New York — a 25-minute ride past the Statue of Liberty and the downtown skyline, no ticket, no queue. Ride out, turn around, ride back; go at golden hour.

items.name: Central Park
items.description: The 843-acre green heart of the city — the Bethesda Terrace, the Ramble, the Bow Bridge and the Reservoir loop; hire bikes or a rowboat, or take the kids to the zoo. A different world every season.

items.name: The High Line
items.description: A disused elevated freight line turned wild-planted walkway above the West Side, threading past galleries and river views; walk it end to end and step off into Chelsea's art scene or Hudson Yards.

items.name: Little Island
items.description: A pocket park floating over the Hudson on concrete 'tulips' by Heatherwick — undulating lawns, hidden overlooks and a small amphitheatre with summer performances. Free, and a lovely 20 minutes off the High Line.

items.name: Brooklyn Bridge
items.description: Walk the elevated wooden promenade from Manhattan into Brooklyn for the definitive skyline view; go early morning to have the cathedral-like stone arches nearly to yourself, then descend into DUMBO.

items.name: Brooklyn Bridge Park & DUMBO
items.description: Cobbled streets under the bridge, the Instagram-famous Washington Street view of the Manhattan Bridge, Jane's Carousel and a green waterfront that faces the whole downtown skyline. End the bridge walk here.

items.name: Washington Square Park & Greenwich Village
items.description: The marble arch, the fountain, the chess players and street musicians — the bohemian soul of the city, ringed by NYU and low townhouse streets perfect for aimless wandering.

items.name: The West Village
items.description: Crooked, tree-lined streets of red-brick townhouses, tiny bookshops and cafés — the prettiest walk in Manhattan and the loveliest for an unhurried morning. Bleecker and Perry streets are the postcard.

items.name: SoHo
credentials: SoHo-Cast Iron Historic District — National Historic Landmark
items.description: The world's densest run of cast-iron architecture, now a cobblestoned luxury shopping quarter — flagship boutiques below, ornate 19th-century facades above. Look up as much as into the windows.

items.name: Chinatown & Little Italy
items.description: One of the largest Chinese communities in the West — dim sum, tea shops and produce markets flowing into the last blocks of Little Italy on Mulberry Street; a sensory wander best done hungry.

items.name: The Lower East Side
items.description: The old immigrant tenement district turned gallery-and-cocktail neighbourhood; the Tenement Museum tells the story through restored apartments, then the streets deliver vintage shops and the New Museum.

items.name: Harlem
items.description: The capital of Black American culture — a Sunday gospel service, the Apollo Theater, soul food on Lenox Avenue and the Studio Museum; take a guided walk to read the history in the brownstones.

items.name: Williamsburg
items.description: Brooklyn's design-and-nightlife capital — independent boutiques, rooftop bars and the best Manhattan-skyline sunset in the city from the East River waterfront. Take the ferry over for the arrival.

items.name: The Apollo Theater
items.description: The stage where Ella Fitzgerald, James Brown and Aretha were made — catch the legendary Amateur Night or a show, or take the daytime tour of a true American music landmark.

items.name: Broadway & the Theater District
items.description: The world's benchmark for musical theatre — book a marquee show months ahead through your advisor; family groups can't go wrong with The Lion King or Aladdin. Skip Times Square itself once you've seen it.

items.name: Lincoln Center for the Performing Arts
items.description: The Metropolitan Opera, the New York Philharmonic and City Ballet around a floodlit travertine plaza and fountain — dress up for a Met Opera night, one of the great evenings out in the city.

items.name: Carnegie Hall
items.description: The most storied concert hall in America, with acoustics musicians travel the world to play — a recital here is a bucket-list evening; a backstage tour reveals the history if you can't catch a show.

items.name: Village Vanguard & the Village jazz clubs
items.description: The basement room where Coltrane and Bill Evans recorded live albums — still the holy ground of jazz. Book the early set; pair it with Blue Note or Smalls nearby for a proper night of music.

items.name: Grand Central Terminal
items.description: Not a station so much as a Beaux-Arts cathedral — the celestial-ceiling main concourse, the Whispering Gallery and an oyster bar in the vaults below. Free, always open, and quietly astonishing.

items.name: The New York Public Library (Stephen A. Schwarzman Building)
items.description: The marble-lion library whose Rose Reading Room — a football-field of chandeliers and painted clouds — is open to anyone who walks in; catch a free treasures exhibition and step next door into Bryant Park.

items.name: Rockefeller Center
items.description: An Art Deco city-within-a-city — the golden Prometheus and the sunken plaza (ice-skating in winter, the giant tree in December), Radio City next door and Top of the Rock above. The heart of Midtown.

items.name: St. Patrick's Cathedral
items.description: The great white Gothic-Revival cathedral facing Rockefeller Center — step in from the Fifth Avenue bustle for the soaring nave and rose window; a five-minute pause that resets the whole day.

items.name: The Oculus & World Trade Center
items.description: Calatrava's soaring white-ribbed transit hall — like a bird or a whale's skeleton in marble — now a luxury shopping concourse; the most dramatic piece of new architecture downtown, and free to walk through.

items.name: Chelsea gallery district
items.description: The world's densest concentration of contemporary art galleries — Gagosian, David Zwirner, Hauser & Wirth and dozens more, all free to enter. Spend a Saturday afternoon drifting between shows off the High Line.

items.name: Chelsea Market
items.description: A former Nabisco biscuit factory turned covered food hall — lobster, tacos, artisan pastry and design shops in brick-and-pipe arcades; graze your way through, then step straight onto the High Line above.

items.name: Grand Central Market & Great Northern Food Hall
items.description: Within and beside the terminal — a European-style market of cheese, seafood and fresh bread, and Nordic food stalls under the arches. A civilised graze while you admire the building.

items.name: Smorgasburg
items.description: America's largest open-air food market — a hundred-odd vendors of everything from ramen burgers to mango sticky rice, with the Manhattan skyline behind. Weekends only, and a great way to eat your way through Brooklyn.

items.name: Fifth Avenue & Madison Avenue shopping
items.description: The full spectrum of luxury — the marquee flagships and Bergdorf Goodman on Fifth, the quieter European maisons and galleries up Madison. Your advisor can arrange private appointments and after-hours access.

items.name: SoHo boutiques
items.description: The most stylish shopping in the city — flagship fashion, concept stores and independent design along cast-iron blocks; less crowded and more curated than Fifth Avenue, and made for wandering on foot.

items.name: A Central Park bike or pedicab ride
items.description: The loveliest way to see the whole park in an hour — hire bikes at Columbus Circle, or take a guided pedicab to the film locations and hidden corners. Gentler and more private than the carriage horses.

items.name: A Hudson River sunset sail
items.description: Board a classic schooner or private yacht for a sail past the Statue of Liberty as the skyline lights up — the single most romantic hour in New York, and easily chartered privately through your advisor.

items.name: A Manhattan helicopter tour
items.description: Fifteen minutes over the harbour, the Statue of Liberty and the length of the skyline — the view that puts the whole city in one frame; ask your advisor about doors-off or private charters.

items.name: The Roosevelt Island Tramway
items.description: A commuter aerial cable-car — on a subway swipe — that glides over the East River beside the Queensboro Bridge for a five-minute skyline ride; a quiet thrill most visitors never find.

items.name: Prospect Park & the Brooklyn Botanic Garden
items.description: The same designers' 'better' park than Central Park — meadows, a lake and a ravine with fewer crowds — beside a botanic garden famed for its spring cherry blossom and Japanese pond. A perfect Brooklyn morning.

items.name: Green-Wood Cemetery
items.description: A 478-acre Victorian garden cemetery of rolling hills, glacial ponds and Gothic gates — resting place of Basquiat and Bernstein, with the best hidden harbour view in Brooklyn. Wildly atmospheric and almost empty.

items.name: The Cathedral of St. John the Divine
items.description: The largest Gothic cathedral in the world, still famously unfinished — a vast, cool, half-built nave with a peacock in the close. Deeply atmospheric, and paired well with a Columbia University stroll.

items.name: The Tenement Museum
items.description: Restored immigrant apartments in a preserved 1863 tenement, told through the real families who lived there — the most moving history lesson in the city, and resonant for anyone whose own family emigrated. Book a tour ahead.

items.name: Storm King Art Center
items.description: A 500-acre open-air sculpture park where monumental Calders, Serras and Goldsworthys sit in rolling meadows and woods — a full day of art and landscape; hire bikes on arrival. A superb warm-weather day trip.

items.name: Dia Beacon
items.description: A former Nabisco box factory turned vast, daylit museum of minimalist and land art — Richter, Serra, Judd on a monumental scale. Reachable by a scenic Metro-North ride along the Hudson; the most serene art day out.

items.name: The Hamptons
items.description: The summer-weekend playground of Manhattan's elite — ocean beaches, hedge-lined estates, farm stands and East Hampton village; best mid-week to avoid the crowds. Your advisor can arrange a house or a beach club.

items.name: Eleven Madison Park
items.description: Daniel Humm's plant-based three-star — the most talked-about fine-dining room in America.

items.name: Le Bernardin
items.description: Eric Ripert's temple to seafood — three stars held for decades, and never a slip.

items.name: Per Se
items.description: Thomas Keller's New York flagship — a hushed room over Central Park, at the summit.

items.name: Jungsik
items.description: Yim Jungsik's modern Korean — the cuisine reimagined at the very highest level.

items.name: Sushi Sho
items.description: The city's newest three-star — a revered Tokyo master's edomae omakase.

items.name: Atomix
items.description: The Parks' Korean tasting counter — named the best restaurant in North America.

items.name: Masa
items.description: Masa Takayama's austere, extravagant sushi — still among the costliest meals in America.

items.name: Daniel
items.description: Daniel Boulud's grand French dining room — the Upper East Side's most elegant table.

items.name: Jean-Georges
items.description: Jean-Georges Vongerichten's flagship — light, precise French with a park view.

items.name: The Modern
items.description: Refined American cooking overlooking MoMA's sculpture garden — art on both sides of the glass.

items.name: Gabriel Kreuther
items.description: Alsatian-French cooking of real soul, overlooking Bryant Park.

items.name: Aska
items.description: Fredrik Berselius's Nordic tasting menu in a candlelit Williamsburg townhouse.

items.name: Atera
items.description: An intimate Tribeca counter of exacting, seasonal tasting menus.

items.name: Saga
items.description: A tasting menu high in a landmark 1930s skyscraper — the view is part of the meal.

items.name: César
items.description: A French-Japanese two-star that arrived fully formed — precise and personal.

items.name: Chef's Table at Brooklyn Fare
items.description: An intense, seafood-led counter — one of the city's most serious tasting experiences.

items.name: Joo Ok
items.description: A refined Korean tasting menu, newly elevated to two stars — quiet, considered, exact.

items.name: Sushi Noz
items.description: A hinoki-wood counter of pure edomae craft — sushi as meditation.

items.name: Odo
items.description: A serene kaiseki counter hidden behind a tea room — Japan, faithfully rendered.

items.name: Huso
items.description: A caviar-and-seafood tasting counter of great luxury — newly starred.

items.name: Aquavit
items.description: The city's benchmark for Nordic cooking — cool, clean, and quietly luxurious.

items.name: Semma
items.description: The only Indian restaurant in America to hold a Michelin star — South India, uncompromised.

items.name: Café Carmellini
items.description: Andrew Carmellini's grand, romantic Italian-French room inside The Fifth Avenue Hotel.

items.name: Torrisi
items.description: Italian-American cooking with a New-York swagger, in the landmark Puck Building.

items.name: Rezdôra
items.description: A love letter to Emilia-Romagna — the city's most wanted pasta.

items.name: Le Coucou
items.description: A beautiful, candlelit ode to classical French cooking in the heart of SoHo.

items.name: Crown Shy
items.description: James Kent's downtown room — inventive, generous, and consistently excellent.

items.name: The Dining Room at Gramercy Tavern
items.description: A New York institution — seasonal American cooking of unwavering grace.

items.name: COTE
items.description: A Korean steakhouse of real refinement — the butcher's counter meets the tasting menu.

items.name: Le Pavillon
items.description: Daniel Boulud's soaring, garden-like room of vegetable- and seafood-led French cooking.

items.name: Café Boulud at Maison Barnes
items.description: Daniel Boulud's warm, seasonal café — refined French with an easy grace.

items.name: Sushi Nakazawa
items.description: A joyful, generous omakase from a Jiro-trained master — sushi with a smile.

items.name: Corima
items.description: Modern Northern Mexican cooking that earned a star within a year of opening.

items.name: Dirt Candy
items.description: Amanda Cohen's pioneering vegetable tasting menu — the case for vegetables, made joyfully.

items.name: The Four Horsemen
items.description: A wine bar that quietly became one of the country's best restaurants.

items.name: Bridges
items.description: A newly-starred Chinatown room bringing quiet French finesse to a downtown corner.

items.name: Yamada
items.description: A precise new Japanese counter that earned its star straight out of the gate.

items.name: Frevo
items.description: An intimate tasting menu hidden behind an art-gallery door — French with a Brazilian pulse.

items.name: Kono
items.description: A tiny yakitori counter of great purity — every part of the bird over charcoal.

items.name: Le Veau d'Or
items.description: New York's oldest French bistro, lovingly revived — a piece of the city's soul.

items.name: Oxomoco
items.description: Wood-fired, one-star Mexican cooking in a sunlit Greenpoint room.

items.name: Via Carota
items.description: The West Village trattoria everyone wants a table at — simple, perfect, always full.

items.name: Dhamaka
items.description: Unapologetic, rustic Indian cooking that pulls no punches — a love letter to the regions.

items.name: Bungalow
items.description: Vikas Khanna's ode to Indian country-club dining — glamorous, generous, joyful.

items.name: Cardamom
items.description: Modern Indian cooking with a light, contemporary hand — Bib-listed and easy to love.

items.name: Chutney Masala
items.description: Warm, well-made Indian cooking that quietly earned the inspectors' nod.

items.name: HanGawi
items.description: A serene, shoes-off Korean temple restaurant — entirely vegetarian, and quietly special.

items.name: Coqodaq
items.description: A glamorous Korean fried-chicken-and-Champagne room — serious fun, seriously good.

items.name: Bonnie's
items.description: Cantonese-American cooking with a Brooklyn wit — nostalgic and inventive at once.

items.name: Atla
items.description: Bright, all-day Mexican cooking from the Cosme team — fresh, light, and always buzzing.

items.name: Dim Sum Go Go
items.description: A Chinatown stalwart doing precise, handmade dim sum — credentialed and beloved.

items.name: CheLi
items.description: Shanghainese home cooking done with real care — a Bib-listed crowd favourite.

items.name: Bemelmans Bar
credentials: A globally historic cocktail bar, inside The Carlyle
items.description: The most beautiful bar in New York — Ludwig Bemelmans' murals, a grand piano, a perfect martini.

items.name: The King Cole Bar
credentials: A globally historic cocktail bar, inside The St. Regis
items.description: The birthplace of the Bloody Mary, beneath Maxfield Parrish's mural — old-money New York.

items.name: The Dead Rabbit
items.description: A former World's Best Bar reviving the lost art of the New York-Irish tavern.

items.name: Katana Kitten
credentials: Former World's Best Bar in America
items.description: A Japanese-American izakaya bar that has ranked among the world's best for years.

items.name: Double Chicken Please
credentials: World's 50 Best Bars — former No. 1 in North America
items.description: An inventive back-room bar that was recently ranked the best in North America.

items.name: Attaboy
items.description: A no-menu speakeasy where you name a spirit and a mood — bespoke drinks, no fuss.

items.name: The Aviary NYC
credentials: A bar of international standing, from the Alinea Group
items.description: A theatrical cocktail laboratory high in the Mandarin Oriental — drinks as edible art.

items.name: Overstory
items.description: Cocktails on the 64th floor with a 360-degree sweep of the harbour and the skyline.

items.name: The Rooftop at Pier 17
credentials: A landmark rooftop venue at the Seaport
items.description: Drinks and skyline views by the Brooklyn Bridge — the river breeze on a summer night.

items.name: Employees Only
items.description: A speakeasy that helped start the modern cocktail revival — buzzy well past midnight.

items.title: A private evening at the Met or MoMA
items.description: A curator-led walk of the galleries after closing, the collection quiet and yours.

items.title: The tasting menu at a top-tier Manhattan table
items.description: The three-star rooms and the impossible reservations an advisor can actually secure.

items.title: A helicopter loop over Manhattan at dusk
items.description: The skyline, the bridges and the harbour from the air as the lights come on.

items.title: A night in a Broadway house with the best seats and a backstage visit

items.name: Tribeca / SoHo
items.description: Cast-iron loft streets, galleries and the best downtown dining; suits design lovers and repeat visitors.

items.name: West Village
items.description: Leafy, low-rise and romantic, with the city's most walkable streets; suits couples and anyone wanting charm over spectacle.

items.name: Upper East Side
items.description: Museum Mile, Central Park and the grand old hotels; suits families and first-timers who want the classic uptown address.

events.name: Tribeca Festival
events.note: Robert De Niro's downtown film festival, when premieres and talks take over lower Manhattan for a fortnight.

events.name: US Open (tennis)
events.note: The season's final Grand Slam in Flushing Meadows, the loudest and latest-running of the four.

events.name: Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade
events.note: The giant-balloon parade down Central Park West on Thanksgiving morning, the start of the city's holiday season.

onGround.heading: On the ground

rows.label: Arriving
rows.value: Arrive at JFK or Newark (EWR); a pre-booked black car or a member service like Blade's helicopter transfer from JFK avoids the bridge-and-tunnel crawl into Manhattan.

rows.label: Getting around
rows.value: Manhattan is best walked, with a private car or well-vetted black-car app for cross-town and downtown moves; skip driving yourself.

rows.label: Connectivity
rows.value: US eSIM (AT&T/Verizon/T-Mobile) or an international eSIM works everywhere; coverage and hotel Wi-Fi are excellent, subway signal now included.

rows.label: Money
rows.value: US dollar; cards and Apple Pay are universal and cash is rarely needed; tip roughly 20% at restaurants and $2–5 per bag or service.

onGround.note: Stay in the low 60s off Central Park or in the West Village for quiet luxury; the ESTA must be secured before an Indian passport holder travels, and dinner at the best tables (or a Broadway premiere) needs booking weeks ahead.

rows.label: Climate
rows.value: Late April-June and September-October are the kind windows, mild and clear; avoid the humid heat of July-August and the deep cold and slush of January-February.

rows.label: Flights from India
rows.value: Air India flies Delhi-New York (JFK and Newark) nonstop in about 15-16 hours, with United and American also nonstop from Delhi; from Mumbai and Bengaluru it is typically one stop via a Gulf or European hub in J or F. If connecting, Emirates via Dubai offers the strongest first-class and lounge experience.

rows.label: Health & safety
rows.value: No vaccinations required beyond routine; the ESTA or B-1/B-2 visa must be arranged in advance for the Indian passport. Manhattan is safe with ordinary big-city awareness. Tap water is excellent.

rows.label: Dining, veg & Jain
rows.value: Vegetarian is effortless and Jain is achievable in the Indian restaurants; the city has serious Indian dining. Consider Dhamaka or Semma (Michelin-starred South Indian) for something beyond the ordinary.

seo.title: Nice & the Riviera — TripAgent
seo.description: Nice & the Riviera, in hand: where to stay, what to do, where to eat and where the night goes — the addresses worth knowing.

hero.name: Nice & the Riviera
hero.tagline: Belle Époque glamour along the azure Mediterranean coast.

ourTake.lede: Nice is the right base for the Riviera — better value and more real life than Cannes or Monaco, and everything is a short train ride away. Skip the pebble beach for the old town and the Cimiez hills; the daily Cours Saleya market and a Niçoise lunch beat any beach club. Use the coastal train as your car: Villefranche, Èze and Menton are all quick hops, and the corniche drives are the day out worth renting for.
ourTake.comeIf: You want the Riviera: the sea, the light, and Monaco and Cannes at hand.
ourTake.skipIf: You want budget or solitude; this coast trades on glamour and it prices accordingly.
