Leopard resting on rock beside tree trunk

whenToGo.blurb: December to March is warm and euphoric, crowned by Carnival and Reveillon; the heat and crowds peak then, so book far ahead or come in the milder shoulders.
whenToGo.bestMonths: Jan, Feb, Mar, Sep, Oct, Nov and Dec

guide.lede: Where to stay, what to do, where to eat, and where the night goes — grouped by price, every address earned by a name worth trusting.

items.name: Copacabana Palace, A Belmond Hotel
items.description: The 1923 palace on Copacabana's seafront — the definitive grand hotel of South America, and still the city's most storied address.

items.name: Fasano Rio de Janeiro
credentials: The Leading Hotels of the World
items.description: Philippe Starck's dark, glamorous high-rise over Ipanema — a rooftop infinity pool and one of the great beach-front views in the city.

items.name: Hotel Emiliano Rio
items.description: A contemporary Brazilian-modernist house over Copacabana Beach — a rooftop pool, a spa and quietly impeccable service.

items.name: Fairmont Rio de Janeiro Copacabana
items.description: At the head of Copacabana Beach — a full-service grand hotel with the finest uninterrupted sweep of the bay's white sand.

items.name: JANEIRO Hotel
items.description: Designer-hotelier Oskar Metsavaht's house over Leblon Beach — Brazilian timber, sculptural furniture and floor-to-ceiling sea and sky.

items.name: Hotel Emiliano — beachfront suites (Copacabana)
items.description: The suite tier of the Emiliano — larger, sea-facing rooms with the same modernist restraint and rooftop-pool access.

items.name: Santa Teresa Hotel RJ — MGallery
items.description: A restored hillside coffee estate in bohemian Santa Teresa — Brazilian modernist design, hardwoods and a hilltop pool above the city.

items.name: Sofitel Rio de Janeiro Copacabana
items.description: A grand French-flavoured house between Copacabana and Arpoador — two rooftop pools and one of the best sunset outlooks in the city.

items.name: Miramar Hotel by Windsor
items.description: A polished mid-century tower on the Copacabana seafront with a much-loved rooftop bar over the beach.

items.name: Christ the Redeemer & Corcovado
credentials: New7Wonders of the World — Christ the Redeemer
UNESCO World Heritage Site — Rio de Janeiro: Carioca Landscapes between the Mountain and the Sea
items.description: The 30-metre Art Deco statue crowns Corcovado at 710 metres, arms open over the whole city. Ride the century-old cog train up through rainforest, or arrange a private guide who can time your arrival for the softer early light and thinner crowds, and let elders take the panoramic lift rather than the final steps.

items.name: The Corcovado Train (Trem do Corcovado)
items.description: Brazil's oldest tourist railway, running since 1884, climbs 3.8 kilometres of steep track through Tijuca forest to the foot of the statue. The twenty-minute ascent past waterfalls and tree canopy is an experience in itself, and children tend to remember the little red train as much as the view.

items.name: Sugarloaf Mountain (Pão de Açúcar)
credentials: UNESCO World Heritage Site — Rio de Janeiro: Carioca Landscapes between the Mountain and the Sea
items.description: Two glass cable cars glide from Praia Vermelha up Morro da Urca and on to the 396-metre granite dome, opening a 360-degree sweep of Guanabara Bay, Copacabana and Christ on his distant peak. Time the second car for sunset, when the whole city turns amber and then lights up. The cableway has run since 1912.

items.name: Copacabana Beach & the Copacabana Palace
credentials: UNESCO World Heritage Site — Rio de Janeiro: Carioca Landscapes between the Mountain and the Sea
items.description: Four kilometres of crescent sand framed by the Portuguese-wave promenade, with the grande-dame Copacabana Palace watching over it since 1923. Take an early-morning walk before the heat, then a discreet lunch on the hotel terrace; the beach itself is best enjoyed with a guide and your valuables left in the room.

items.name: Ipanema Beach & the Fasano
credentials: UNESCO World Heritage Site — Rio de Janeiro: Carioca Landscapes between the Mountain and the Sea
items.description: The most stylish stretch of Rio, immortalised by the bossa-nova song, with the Dois Irmãos peaks closing the western end. The Fasano's rooftop pool and its Italian dining room are the natural base for a discreet family; posto 9 is the see-and-be-seen sand, quieter towards Leblon.

items.name: Arpoador Sunset
items.description: The rocky point between Ipanema and Copacabana where cariocas gather each evening to watch the sun drop behind Dois Irmãos, and applaud when it does. Have your driver drop you close by; it is one of the city's genuine communal rituals and costs nothing.

items.name: Selarón Steps (Escadaria Selarón)
items.description: The 215 steps that Chilean artist Jorge Selarón spent two decades tiling with more than 2,000 ceramics from around the world, including many from India and Brazil. A short, vivid stop between Lapa and Santa Teresa, best in mid-morning before the crowds thicken.

items.name: Santa Teresa & the Bonde Tram
items.description: Rio's bohemian hilltop quarter of cobbled lanes, artists' studios and colonial mansions, reached by the restored yellow bonde tram over the Lapa aqueduct. Book a table at a hillside restaurant with a bay view; it is the most atmospheric neighbourhood in the city and easy to explore slowly with a private guide.

items.name: The Lapa Arches (Arcos da Lapa) & Nightlife
items.description: The 18th-century white aqueduct is the emblem of Lapa, the district that comes alive after dark with samba clubs and street music. Best appreciated lit up in the evening; a guide can frame a safe hour or two of live samba at a reputable house without wading into the crush.

items.name: Maracanã Stadium
items.description: The temple of Brazilian football, host of two World Cup finals and the 2016 Olympic ceremonies. A behind-the-scenes tour of the pitch, dressing rooms and trophy hall lands well with sports-loving teenagers; catching a match with a guide is unforgettable but best arranged with security in mind.

items.name: Museum of Tomorrow (Museu do Amanhã)
items.description: Santiago Calatrava's spectacular white pavilion juts over the water like a great bird, its interactive science exhibits on climate and the future built for curious minds of every age. The anchor of the revitalised port district and a strong wet-weather option for multi-generational groups.

items.name: Museu de Arte do Rio (MAR)
items.description: Two contrasting buildings joined by a wave-form roof on Praça Mauá, showing Brazilian art and the city's own story. Pair it with the Museum of Tomorrow across the square for a half-day of culture in the reborn port.

items.name: Olympic Boulevard & the Kobra Etnias Mural
items.description: The revitalised waterfront promenade of the 2016 Games, anchored by Eduardo Kobra's vast 'Etnias' mural of five indigenous faces from five continents, once the world's largest spray-paint artwork. An open-air stroll that pairs street art with harbour views.

items.name: Rio Botanical Garden (Jardim Botânico)
credentials: UNESCO World Heritage Site — Rio de Janeiro: Carioca Landscapes between the Mountain and the Sea
items.description: Founded by the Portuguese crown in 1808, 140 hectares of avenues of imperial palms, orchid houses and giant Amazonian water lilies at the foot of Corcovado. Cool, shaded and gentle underfoot, it is ideal for grandparents and small children on a hot afternoon.

items.name: Parque Lage
items.description: A dreamlike Italianate mansion with a courtyard café set against the sheer rock of Corcovado, the statue framed perfectly above the arches. Wander the English gardens, take coffee in the courtyard, and start the walking trail toward Christ if the fit want to.

items.name: Tijuca National Park
credentials: UNESCO World Heritage Site — Rio de Janeiro: Carioca Landscapes between the Mountain and the Sea
items.description: One of the world's largest urban rainforests, hand-replanted in the 19th century, with waterfalls, the Cascatinha Taunay, jungle trails and toucans within the city limits. A private 4x4 tour lets a whole family reach the peaks and pools without a demanding hike.

items.name: Vista Chinesa
items.description: An Oriental-style stone pavilion perched in the Tijuca forest, giving one of the finest framed panoramas of the lagoon, Ipanema and Christ from a single balcony. An easy drive-up viewpoint that rewards a five-minute stop on the way through the park.

items.name: Theatro Municipal
items.description: Rio's belle-époque opera house of 1909, modelled on the Paris Opéra, all marble, gilt and Carrara staircases. Take a guided daytime tour of the auditorium and foyers, or dress for an evening of ballet or opera under the great chandelier.

items.name: Confeitaria Colombo
items.description: A gilded-age tea room from 1894 with Belgian mirrors, jacaranda counters and stained glass, the most beautiful café in Brazil. Afternoon tea here is a genteel institution, and the pastries and salgados are easy for a vegetarian to navigate.

items.name: Royal Portuguese Reading Room (Real Gabinete Português de Leitura)
items.description: A neo-Manueline jewel-box library of 1887 holding the largest collection of Portuguese literature outside Portugal, its galleried hall often named among the world's most beautiful. A short, hushed, breathtaking visit for anyone who loves books and design.

items.name: Candelária Church
items.description: The great domed baroque-and-neoclassical church at the heart of downtown, its Italian marble interior a cool refuge amid the city bustle. A quick, dignified stop on any Centro walking tour.

items.name: Niterói Contemporary Art Museum (MAC)
items.description: Oscar Niemeyer's flying-saucer museum of 1996, poised on a cliff above a reflecting pool, its ramp curling toward a wall of glass. Cross Guanabara Bay for the building itself and for the return view of Rio's skyline; the drive over the great bridge is half the pleasure.

items.name: Pedra do Telégrafo
items.description: The cliff-edge rock whose optical illusion makes hikers appear to dangle over a vast abyss when in fact the drop is small. A moderate hour-and-a-half trail out west rewards fit teenagers and photographers with the city's most shared image.

items.name: Hang-Gliding off Pedra Bonita
items.description: A tandem launch from the 510-metre Pedra Bonita ramp inside Tijuca park, soaring past Pedra da Gávea and the ocean before landing on São Conrado beach. The city's signature adventure for the bold, flights lasting eight to twelve minutes with a certified pilot.

items.name: Prainha Beach
items.description: A protected crescent of golden sand backed by Atlantic rainforest, favoured by surfers and cariocas escaping the city crowds. Wilder and quieter than the postcard beaches, it makes a good half-day out west with a driver.

items.name: Grumari Beach
items.description: A wide, undeveloped stretch inside an environmental reserve, with reddish sand, forested hills and no high-rises. One of the last unspoilt beaches within the city, best paired with Prainha and lunch at a rustic seafood shack.

items.name: Barra da Tijuca Beach
items.description: Rio's longest beach, nearly 18 kilometres of open sand fronting the modern, spacious district that hosted the Olympics. Calmer and more suburban than Ipanema, with malls and family restaurants nearby, it suits travellers who want room to breathe.

items.name: A Favela Cultural Visit
items.description: Communities such as those linked to social projects can be visited on respectful, community-led tours that support local artists, cooks and guides rather than treating residents as a spectacle. Go only with a reputable operator who lives or works there; it is a way to understand the real city, not a photo safari.

items.name: Feira de São Cristóvão
items.description: A vast covered fair celebrating the culture of Brazil's northeast, with live forró music, food stalls and craft. Lively and colourful, especially at weekends; a guide helps a family navigate it and find the vegetarian-friendly corn and cassava dishes.

items.name: The Sambadrome (Sambódromo Marquês de Sapucaí)
items.description: Niemeyer's 700-metre parade avenue, built in 1984, where the samba schools compete over four Carnival nights before 90,000 spectators. Out of season you can tour it and its Carnival museum; in season, a private box turns the world's greatest show into a comfortable, secure night.

items.name: A Samba Night
items.description: Live samba is the soul of Rio, from the roda at Pedra do Sal in the old port to polished houses in Lapa. A guide can seat a family at a reputable venue for a couple of hours of music and dance without navigating the late-night crush alone.

items.name: Escadaria & Largo do Boticário
items.description: A tiny, storybook square of pastel colonial houses tucked into the forest near the Corcovado train station, one of Rio's most photographed hidden corners. A quiet, atmospheric pause to fold into a Corcovado morning.

items.name: Mirante Dona Marta
items.description: A road-accessible balcony below Christ the Redeemer giving a clean, elevated line over Botafogo, Sugarloaf and the bay, and back up at the statue itself. The go-to viewpoint for photographers who want the whole composition without a hike.

items.name: Rodrigo de Freitas Lagoon (Lagoa)
credentials: UNESCO World Heritage Site — Rio de Janeiro: Carioca Landscapes between the Mountain and the Sea
items.description: The saltwater lagoon ringed by an eight-kilometre path, hemmed by Ipanema, the Botanical Garden and the hills, with kiosks and pedalos. A gentle sunset stroll, cycle or waterside dinner that shows Rio at its most relaxed and family-friendly.

items.name: Escadaria to Dois Irmãos (Morro Dois Irmãos)
items.description: The twin-peak hike above Leblon that delivers arguably the best view in Rio, the whole southern coastline laid out below. A short but steep community-supported trail from Vidigal; go early with a local guide for the light and the safety.

items.name: Petrópolis — the Imperial City
items.description: An hour and a half up into cool mountain air, the 19th-century summer capital of Brazil's emperors, with the Imperial Museum in Pedro II's palace and the Gothic cathedral holding his tomb. A refined change of pace and climate, and a fine multi-generational day out by private car.

items.name: Búzios
items.description: A former fishing village turned chic beach resort of cobbled lanes, boutiques and more than twenty coves, once put on the map by Brigitte Bardot. Two to three hours east; better as an overnight, with elegant pousadas and boat days for a family that wants sun and calm water.

items.name: Ilha Grande & Angra dos Reis
credentials: UNESCO World Heritage Site — Paraty and Ilha Grande: Culture and Biodiversity
items.description: A car-free tropical island of rainforest and turquoise bays reached from the port of Angra dos Reis, best explored by private schooner among hundreds of islands. A long day from Rio, so an overnight and a chartered boat suit a family wanting the Green Coast at leisure.

items.name: Paraty — the UNESCO Colonial Town
credentials: UNESCO World Heritage Site — Paraty and Ilha Grande: Culture and Biodiversity
items.description: A perfectly preserved 18th-century gold-route port of whitewashed churches and cobbled streets that flood at high tide, ringed by waterfalls and Atlantic forest. Four hours from Rio and well worth an overnight; refined pousadas, cachaça distilleries and schooner trips make it a highlight of the Costa Verde.

items.name: Escadaria & the Urca Waterfront
items.description: The village-like neighbourhood at Sugarloaf's foot, where locals sit on the Mureta da Urca sea wall at dusk with a cold drink and the bay before them. A serene, safe pocket of old Rio to end a Sugarloaf visit before dinner.

items.name: Pedra da Gávea
items.description: The colossal 842-metre monolith looming over São Conrado, one of the highest ocean-front peaks in the world, its summit a demanding scramble with an unrivalled reward. Strictly for fit, experienced walkers with a guide; the rest can admire it from the hang-glider ramp.

items.name: Escadaria & the Real Cabinet Quarter — Praça XV
items.description: The old imperial waterfront square where the royal family once landed, with the Paço Imperial palace, the arch to Travessa do Comércio and ferries to Niterói. A handsome starting point for a walking tour of colonial Rio, and the departure quay for the bay crossing.

items.name: Leblon Beach & Neighbourhood
credentials: UNESCO World Heritage Site — Rio de Janeiro: Carioca Landscapes between the Mountain and the Sea
items.description: The quieter, more residential and upscale continuation of Ipanema, with the city's best restaurants and a family-friendly stretch of sand known as Baixo Bebê. The calm base of choice for travellers who want fine dining and a gentler beach scene.

items.name: Museu do Amanhã Gardens & Aquário AquaRio
items.description: Beside the reborn port sits AquaRio, South America's largest marine aquarium, with a walk-through ocean tunnel that delights younger children. An easy, air-conditioned pairing with the Museum of Tomorrow when the family needs an indoor afternoon.

items.name: Lasai
items.description: Rafael Costa e Silva's vegetable-led room in a Botafogo townhouse — the most celebrated table in Rio, sourced from its own gardens.

items.name: Oro
credentials: Latin America's 50 Best Restaurants (former One To Watch)
items.description: Felipe Bronze's theatre of fire and Brazilian ingredients — an inventive, hands-on tasting-menu experience, two Michelin stars strong.

items.name: Oteque
items.description: Alberto Landgraf's precise, seafood-led counter and small dining room — a Japanese-German hand on the finest Brazilian catch.

items.name: Mee
items.description: Pan-Asian fine dining inside the Copacabana Palace — a serene, poolside room and the city's most polished Asian tasting menus.

items.name: Ristorante Hotel Cipriani
credentials: 50 Top Italy — Best Italian restaurant outside Italy
items.description: Chef Nello Cassese's Neapolitan-Piedmontese cooking in a chandeliered room over the palace pool — Italian fine dining of real pedigree.

items.name: Madame Olympe
items.description: A contemporary Brazilian kitchen that earned its first Michelin star in the 2026 guide — assured, personal, of-the-moment.

items.name: Oseille
items.description: Thomas Troisgros's French-Brazilian room above Ipanema — a one-star kitchen from one of Brazil's great culinary families.

items.name: Aprazível
items.description: A hillside garden restaurant in Santa Teresa — modern Brazilian cooking under the trees with a sweeping view over Guanabara Bay.

items.name: Sushi Leblon
items.description: Rio's benchmark Japanese room — a long-standing Leblon fixture for pristine fish and a see-and-be-seen crowd.

items.name: CT Boucherie
items.description: Claude Troisgros's all-you-can-eat parade of grilled cuts and sides — refined churrasco theatre in Leblon.

items.name: Ocyá
items.description: A produce- and fire-led kitchen in Leblon celebrated for its treatment of Brazilian seafood and vegetables.

items.name: Giuseppe Grill
items.description: A carnivore's institution — precise, high-quality Brazilian grilling in an unfussy, always-full room.

items.name: Nosso
items.description: A relaxed three-floor room and cocktail bar in Ipanema — playful modern Brazilian plates and a rooftop terrace.

items.name: Aconchego Carioca
items.description: A warm, much-loved botequim of elevated Carioca home cooking — the famed bolinho de feijoada and a serious cachaça list.

items.name: Confeitaria Colombo
credentials: Historic landmark (est. 1894); named among the world's most beautiful cafés
items.description: Rio's belle-époque grande dame since 1894 — Antwerp mirrors, rosewood and Art Nouveau, for coffee, pastries and old-Rio ceremony.

items.name: Academia da Cachaça
items.description: A Leblon institution since 1985 devoted to cachaça and the caipirinha — the definitive place to learn Brazil's national spirit.

items.name: Confeitaria Colombo (Bar / salon)
items.description: Belle-époque grandeur for an aperitivo among Antwerp mirrors and rosewood — old Rio at its most theatrical.

items.name: Vizinho Gastrobar
items.description: A garden cocktail retreat widely rated among Rio's best bars — refined, fruit-led drinks from a serious bar team.

items.name: Nosso
items.description: A laid-back three-floor bar and kitchen in Ipanema — playful twists on classics drawing on Brazil's distillates and ferments.

items.name: Bar do Copa
credentials: Within Copacabana Palace, A Belmond Hotel
items.description: The polished bar of the Copacabana Palace — impeccable classics and a discreet, grown-up room within the grand old hotel.

items.name: Fasano Rooftop Bar
credentials: Atop Hotel Fasano — MICHELIN Guide Hotel
items.description: The Starck-designed rooftop over Ipanema — a stylish crowd, an infinity pool and one of the great beachfront outlooks in Rio.

items.name: Miramar Rooftop (Windsor Miramar)
credentials: Atop the Miramar Hotel — MICHELIN Guide Hotel
items.description: A much-loved rooftop bar directly over Copacabana Beach — a classic Carioca vantage on the great arc of sand.

items.name: Lapa (Rio Scenarium & the arches)
credentials: Landmark Rio nightlife district; Rio Scenarium is a celebrated live-music house
items.description: Rio's samba heartland beneath the aqueduct arches — live music, dancing and the antique-filled halls of Rio Scenarium.

items.title: Helicopter over Christ the Redeemer
items.description: A short flight banks around the statue and Sugarloaf with the bays laid out beneath you.

items.title: Sunset flight up Sugarloaf's second car
items.description: Time the cable car so you top out as the light turns on Guanabara Bay.

items.title: Hang-glide off Pedra Bonita
items.description: A tandem launch from the ridge above São Conrado glides you down to the beach.

items.title: Private sail past the Cagarras Islands
items.description: A skippered day offshore from Ipanema, swimming off the boat away from the crowds.

plan.heading: 4 days in Rio de Janeiro, done well
plan.lede: A day-by-day shape for the trip — the pace we would set. Your advisor books the flights and the rooms; the days are yours.

slots.label: Morning
slots.text: Settle into the Fasano or Copacabana Palace, then a morning walk along Ipanema.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.text: Sunset at Arpoador rock and the shops of Ipanema's Garcia d'Ávila.

slots.label: Evening
slots.text: Dinner at the Fasano's Al Mare, then a caipirinha overlooking the sand.

slots.label: Morning
slots.text: An early private car to Christ the Redeemer atop Corcovado before the haze.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.text: The ateliers and cobbled lanes of Santa Teresa, lunch at Aprazível with the view.

slots.label: Evening
slots.text: Dinner at Lasai in Botafogo, Rio's tasting-menu leader.

slots.label: Morning
slots.text: The cable car up Sugarloaf (Pão de Açúcar) for the bay at its clearest.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.text: A sail across Guanabara Bay, or the botanical garden's palm avenue.

slots.label: Evening
slots.text: Dinner at Oteque in Botafogo, among Latin America's fifty best.

slots.label: Morning
slots.text: A morning in the Tijuca rainforest, the world's largest urban forest, with a guide.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.text: A last afternoon at Leblon beach and a beachside lunch.

slots.label: Evening
slots.text: A final table at Oro in Leblon to close the visit.

cta.label: Have your advisor arrange the stay

items.name: Leblon
items.description: The quieter, moneyed end of the beachfront; best for those wanting calm and good restaurants.

items.name: Ipanema
items.description: The classic address — walkable, lively, close to everything; suits first-timers who want the pulse.

items.name: Santa Teresa
items.description: Hilltop, arty and villa-lined above the centre; for travellers who prefer character to beach access.

events.name: Réveillon (New Year's Eve on Copacabana)
events.note: Two million in white on the sand for fireworks and offerings to the sea goddess Iemanjá.

events.name: Rio Carnival
events.note: The Sambadrome parades plus hundreds of free street blocos across the city.

events.name: Festa de São Sebastião
events.note: The city's patron-saint day, marked by a procession through the centre.

onGround.heading: On the ground

rows.label: Arriving
rows.value: Arrive into Rio's Galeão International (GIG), about 40 minutes from the beachfront; a vetted private car and driver should meet you, which is the sensible standard here.

rows.label: Getting around
rows.value: A trusted private driver throughout; the promenades of Ipanema and Leblon are beautiful to walk by day, but arrange cars after dark rather than hailing.

rows.label: Connectivity
rows.value: Brazilian eSIMs (Vivo, Claro via Airalo) work well in the city; hotel wifi is reliable.

rows.label: Money
rows.value: Brazilian reais; cards and contactless are widely accepted; carry modest cash and tip around 10 percent (often already added as serviço).

onGround.note: Stay in Leblon or the quieter end of Ipanema, or the Copacabana Palace for grandeur; keep valuables and watches discreet in public, and visit Christ the Redeemer and Sugarloaf early to beat crowds and haze.

rows.label: Climate
rows.value: May to September is dry, warm and clear — the kindest season; December to March is hot, humid and crowded, with sticky heat peaking around the New Year and Carnival.

rows.label: Flights from India
rows.value: No direct service from India; the natural routing is one stop through the Gulf onward across the Atlantic — Emirates via Dubai or Qatar via Doha — or via Europe (Lufthansa, Air France), typically 22-26 hours. Fly the long South Atlantic leg in a lie-flat business seat and break the trip in a flagship Gulf lounge.

rows.label: Health & safety
rows.value: Yellow fever vaccination is recommended for Rio and should be arranged well ahead; add Hepatitis A and typhoid, and drink bottled water. Petty crime and street robbery are real — keep valuables and jewellery out of sight, use hotel cars, and stay to Leblon, Ipanema and vetted areas; avoid favelas unless with a trusted guide.

rows.label: Dining, veg & Jain
rows.value: Vegetarian dining is workable in the affluent southern zone and Jain needs can be met with briefing, though it takes more care than at home. Indian restaurants are few, so lean on your hotel and advisor to arrange pure-veg or Jain meals in advance.

collections.headingHtml: Collections Rio de Janeiro belongs to.
collections.lede: Every place we send you appears here on merit — follow the thread to more like it.

closing.headingHtml: Rio de Janeiro, with someone who knows it.
closing.lede: Your advisor arranges the flights, the rooms and the visa — the trip, handled.

seo.title: Rishikesh — TripAgent
seo.description: Rishikesh, in hand: where to stay, what to do, where to eat and where the night goes — the addresses worth knowing.

hero.name: Rishikesh
hero.tagline: Yoga capital of the world on the upper Ganges.

ourTake.lede: Rishikesh has two faces, the spiritual-yoga town and the adventure-rafting town, and the trick is knowing which you came for and staying on the right bank. For calm, take the quieter upstream side and a serious retreat rather than the backpacker strip near the bridges. Come in the cooler months when the Ganga runs clear and the heat is off; skip the monsoon, when rafting closes.
ourTake.comeIf: You want the Ganges, yoga and a serious wellness retreat within reach of Delhi.
ourTake.skipIf: You drink and want nightlife; the town is largely vegetarian and alcohol-free.

firstLook.heroCaption: Modern pool villa with palms and umbrella

grid.caption: purple allium blooms in soft focus
Leopard resting on rock beside tree trunk

whenToGo.blurb: Spring and autumn bring warm days, cool nights and the year's great yoga gathering; skip peak-summer heat, and note July-August's monsoon closes river rafting.
whenToGo.bestMonths: Jan, Feb, Mar, Apr, Oct, Nov and Dec

guide.lede: Where to stay, what to do, where to eat, and where the night goes — grouped by price, every address earned by a name worth trusting.

note.label: On credentials
note.text: Michelin’s inspectors don’t yet come to Rishikesh. So we don’t pretend a star — we credential its tables the way we’d want to be told: World’s 50 Best, Condé Nast Traveller, and the houses we would send our own family to.

items.name: Ananda in the Himalayas
credentials: Condé Nast Traveller Readers' Choice — repeat World's No.1 / Best Destination Spa (2005–07, 2012, 2019, 2020)
Named World's Best Wellness Retreat by Condé Nast Traveller (2023)
Set in the restored Viceregal Palace of the Maharaja of Tehri Garhwal
items.description: India's first destination spa and one of the world's greatest — a 100-acre Maharaja's estate above the Ganges, built for Ayurveda, yoga and genuine transformation.

items.name: Taj Rishikesh Resort & Spa, Uttarakhand
items.area: Singthali Village (river road, ~30 km from town)
credentials: Taj Hotels luxury resort — 79 rooms, suites and villas (several with private pools)
Jiva Grande Spa and a 20,000 sq ft wellness sanctuary
items.description: A dramatic Himalayan-village resort on a private stretch of the Ganges — Taj polish, a 20,000 sq ft wellness sanctuary and a private river beach.

items.name: The Westin Resort & Spa, Himalayas
credentials: The Westin's first Himalayan resort (Marriott Bonvoy)
141 rooms including royal garden villas with private pools
Built around Westin's six pillars of well-being; Heavenly Spa
items.description: Marriott's Himalayan debut — a wellness-led resort of valley-view rooms, infinity pools and yoga-inspired programming near the world's yoga capital.

items.name: The Roseate Ganges, Rishikesh
credentials: Roseate Hotels & Resorts luxury boutique retreat — 16 villas
Featured by Sleeper Magazine for its design
Aheli spa; 17m infinity pool over the Garhwal foothills
items.description: A design-led boutique retreat of 16 standalone villas on the Ganges — quiet, intimate and beautifully made, with a 17-metre infinity pool over the valley.

items.name: Aloha on the Ganges by Leisure Hotels
items.area: Tapovan / Muni Ki Reti (by Laxman Jhula)
credentials: Leisure Hotels riverside resort — 74 rooms on the Ganga
Opposite Rajaji National Park; walkable to Laxman Jhula & Tapovan
Full-service spa and in-house yoga sessions
items.description: A riverside resort right on the Ganges near Laxman Jhula — well-placed for yoga, rafting and the old-town ghats, with a full-service spa.

items.name: EllBee Ganga View
credentials: Boutique art hotel on the Ganga at Triveni Ghat
Home to The Sitting Elephant rooftop restaurant
Steps from the Triveni Ghat Ganga Aarti
items.description: A boutique art hotel beside the Ganga at Triveni Ghat — rooms above the river, art on every wall and the evening aarti a short walk along the ghat.

items.name: The Ganga Aarti at Parmarth Niketan
items.description: At dusk the largest ashram in Rishikesh gathers hundreds on the marble steps below its giant Shiva statue, and children of the ashram lead the fire prayer to the Ganga in unison — lamps, chanting and the river turning gold. It is the most soulful half-hour in town, and it is free. A private guide can secure a seat close to the priests and time your arrival before the crowd fills the ghat.

items.name: The Maha Aarti at Triveni Ghat
items.description: The grander, busier evening aarti — the town's main bathing ghat where the Ganga, Yamuna and mythic Saraswati are said to meet, ringed by lamplight and thousands of floating diyas. Rawer and more local than Parmarth, it is the fuller picture of a living pilgrim city. Come 30 minutes early; a guide keeps a multi-generation group together through the press.

items.name: Lakshman Jhula & Ram Jhula (the swaying footbridges)
items.description: The two iconic iron suspension bridges over the Ganga are the postcard of Rishikesh — pilgrims, cows, motorbikes and monkeys crossing above the green rush of the river. The century-old Lakshman Jhula has been closed and is being rebuilt, so the walkable pair today are Ram Jhula and the newer Janki Setu. Cross at first light before the heat and the crowds, then take chai on the far bank.

items.name: Janki Setu (the newest glass-floor footbridge)
items.description: The third and newest of the Ganga suspension bridges, with a glass-panel section and an evening light show that draws an easy crowd — a gentle, safe cross for grandparents and children while the older Lakshman Jhula stays shut. Temple bells and river chants carry from both banks. Best at blue hour when the lights come on.

items.name: The Beatles Ashram (Chaurasi Kutia)
credentials: Where the Beatles studied Transcendental Meditation, 1968 — much of the White Album was written here
items.description: The abandoned meditation centre where the Beatles came to study with Maharishi Mahesh Yogi in 1968 and wrote much of the White Album — eighty-four egg-shaped stone meditation cells and a domed hall now swallowed by jungle and covered wall-to-ceiling in vivid graffiti and lyric murals. A rare, atmospheric hour that speaks to any generation. Open 10am–4pm; go early, carry cash for the ticket.

items.name: Parmarth Niketan (the ashram itself)
items.description: Beyond the aarti, the largest ashram in Rishikesh is a serene 1,000-room riverside campus of gardens, temples and a daily rhythm of yoga and satsang — the spiritual centre of the yoga capital. A private darshan and a quiet dawn walk before the day begins is a gentle introduction to ashram life without committing to a stay.

items.name: The International Yoga Festival
credentials: The world's foremost international yoga gathering — held here each March
items.description: For one week each March, Parmarth Niketan hosts the world's foremost yoga gathering — 70-plus hours of classes from master teachers worldwide, meditation, kirtan and discourse from India's leading spiritual voices, on the banks of the Ganga. The single best week to be in the yoga capital. Places and quiet accommodation should be arranged months ahead.

items.name: Swarg Ashram & the ashram belt
items.description: The traffic-free heart of spiritual Rishikesh — a riverside warren of ashrams, temples, book stalls and Gita Bhawan's scripture library, where you can walk barefoot along the Ganga with temple bells for a soundtrack. This is where the yoga-and-meditation world actually lives. An early-morning walk with a guide who knows which ashrams welcome visitors is the way in.

items.name: A private yoga & meditation session on the Ganga
credentials: Rishikesh is widely called the Yoga Capital of the World — an informal but universally used title
items.description: Rishikesh is where modern yoga went global, and a one-to-one dawn practice with a serious teacher on a riverside terrace — pranayama, asana, then silence as the mist lifts off the water — is the reason to come. Far more restorative than a group class. Your advisor can match teacher to level, from a first-timer to a lifelong practitioner.

items.name: Ananda in the Himalayas
credentials: Repeatedly ranked among the world's best destination spas
items.description: One of the world's great destination spas — a 100-acre estate around a Maharaja's palace high in the foothills, with Ganga views, Ayurvedic doctors, and week-long wellness programmes blending Ayurveda, yoga and Vedanta with international therapies. The ultra-luxury benchmark for the region and, for many, the whole reason to visit. Book a structured programme, not just nights, for the full effect.

items.name: The Vashishta Gufa (meditation cave)
items.description: A sixty-foot natural cave where the sage Vashishta is said to have meditated, ending in a Shiva lingam in total darkness — you sit on the mud floor in pitch black and silence, with a small ashram and a quiet Ganga beach just outside. The most profound meditation spot near Rishikesh, and utterly uncrowded. A short drive up the Badrinath road; go mid-morning.

items.name: White-water rafting on the Ganga
items.description: The Ganga above Rishikesh is one of the world's classic rafting rivers — cold, jade-green water threaded with named rapids from gentle Grade I to punchy Grade IV, run in stretches from Shivpuri (16 km) to the advanced Kaudiyala (36 km). Genuinely thrilling and safe with the right operator. Your advisor arranges a private craft, certified guides and a riverbank lunch — not the backpacker crush.

items.name: Bungee jumping & the Giant Swing at Jumpin Heights
credentials: India's highest fixed-platform bungee jump — 83 metres
items.description: India's highest fixed-platform bungee — an 83-metre leap from a cantilever built over a rocky Ganga tributary — plus a Giant Swing that free-falls before arcing across the gorge like a human pendulum. The adrenaline counterpoint to all the serenity, run to genuine safety standards. Perfect for a thrill-seeking teenager while the family watches from the deck.

items.name: The Flying Fox & cliff jumping
items.description: A one-kilometre zip-line that flings you across the river valley at speed, and cliff-jumping into deep Ganga pools at Shivpuri — the fun, lower-commitment end of Rishikesh adventure for a mixed-age group. Best paired with a morning raft. Book through one operator so the day flows and the safety cover is real.

items.name: The Neelkanth Mahadev Temple
items.description: A revered blue-spired Shiva temple high on a forested ridge between two river valleys, marking where Shiva is said to have drunk the ocean's poison and turned his throat blue. The drive up through Rajaji forest is half the pleasure; hardier pilgrims trek 12 km from Ram Jhula. Go early to beat both the heat and the queue.

items.name: The Kunjapuri Devi sunrise
credentials: One of the 52 Shakti Peethas of the goddess
items.description: A hilltop Shakti temple at 1,676 m with the finest sunrise in the region — a 360-degree sweep from the snow peaks of Gangotri, Bandarpunch and Chaukhamba on one side to the Ganga valley and the lights of Rishikesh on the other. One of the 52 shakti-peethas. Drive up in the dark for first light, then walk the ridge down.

items.name: The Tera Manzil (Trimbakeshwar) Temple
items.description: A striking thirteen-storey riverside temple — 'Tera Manzil' means thirteen floors — packed with shrines to countless deities, its terraces climbing above the Ganga to a top-floor view over the bridges and the town. A vivid, colourful hour and a favourite photo spot. Climb barefoot in the cool of the morning.

items.name: The Bharat Mandir
credentials: The oldest temple in Rishikesh — traditionally attributed to Adi Shankaracharya
items.description: The oldest temple in Rishikesh, said to have been established by Adi Shankaracharya, tucked in the bazaar lanes of the old town with a black-stone Vishnu idol and a quiet, unhurried atmosphere far from the tourist bridges. A short, grounding stop that most visitors miss. Best combined with a wander through the old-town markets.

items.name: The cafes of Tapovan
items.description: The hillside above Lakshman Jhula is a warren of rooftop cafes serving good coffee, wood-fired pizza, Israeli and Tibetan food and fresh juice, most with a Ganga view and a slow, barefoot, post-yoga rhythm. The town's social heart between practice sessions. Late afternoon, with the river below and the hills going pink, is the moment.

items.name: Sattvic dining (the meat-and-alcohol-free town)
credentials: A legally alcohol- and meat-free holy town
items.description: Rishikesh and Haridwar are holy towns where meat, eggs, alcohol — and even garlic and onion in strict kitchens — are set aside for pure sattvic food: simple, fresh, vegetarian, cooked to nourish the practice. For a Jain or vegetarian traveller the whole destination is effortless. A private table at an ashram thali or a Tapovan cafe shows the range, from austere to genuinely delicious.

items.name: The Neer Garh Waterfall trek
items.description: A short, pretty forest walk off the Tapovan road climbs past tiered limestone falls to a couple of clear plunge pools where you can cool off — the most accessible of the local waterfalls and an easy morning for a family. Go September to November when the monsoon has filled it. Carry water shoes.

items.name: The Patna Waterfall trek
items.description: A steeper, wilder waterfall trek through forest and past a limestone cave to a 40-foot cascade — quieter and more of a hike than Neer Garh, and often combined with the drive up to Neelkanth. A satisfying half-day for able walkers. Best in the post-monsoon months when the water runs full.

items.name: The Garud Chatti Waterfall
items.description: A hidden, multi-tier fall a short walk from Lakshman Jhula, tucked in green forest and far quieter than the better-known falls — the reward is a private pool and birdsong rather than a crowd. The classic one-day loop links it with Neer Garh and Phool Chatti. A gentle, off-the-map morning.

items.name: Riverside luxury camping at Shivpuri
items.description: White-sand Ganga beaches upriver where premium camps pitch furnished tents by the water — bonfires, star fields, birdcall and a raft run at the door, without the roadside crowds of the town. A magical night for a multi-generation group who want the river without roughing it. Your advisor picks the camp with the beach and the standards to match.

items.name: Phool Chatti Ashram & waterfall
items.description: A tranquil riverbank ashram known for its structured silent-and-yoga retreats, with a small waterfall nearby and a stretch of Ganga far from the day-trippers. The place to go deeper than a single class. Even a day visit conveys the discipline and calm of ashram immersion.

items.name: The Har Ki Pauri Ganga Aarti (Haridwar)
credentials: Haridwar's holiest ghat and the principal Kumbh Mela bathing site
items.description: The grandest Ganga aarti in the country — at Haridwar's holiest ghat, where Vishnu is said to have left a footprint, thousands gather at dusk as giant flaming lamps are swung to roaring bells and the river carries a carpet of leaf-boat diyas downstream. Overwhelming and unforgettable. A guide arranges a safe raised vantage away from the densest crush, essential with elders or children.

items.name: The Mansa Devi Ropeway (Haridwar)
items.description: A cable-car ('udan khatola') swings up the hill to the wish-fulfilling Mansa Devi temple, with the whole spread of Haridwar and the Ganga laid out below — the fast, comfortable alternative to the 3-km climb and a highlight for children. Pair it with the Chandi Devi ropeway across the valley. Go mid-morning after the aarti crowds thin.

items.name: The Chandi Devi Ropeway (Haridwar)
items.description: The second of Haridwar's hilltop goddess shrines, a Siddh Peeth reached by its own cable car over forested ridges — the pair of ropeways make a neat half-day of temple-hopping high above the town. Quieter than Mansa Devi and with wider Himalayan-foothill views. A guide books the combined tickets to skip the lines.

items.name: The Kumbh Mela ground at Haridwar
credentials: Site of the Kumbh Mela — among the largest human gatherings on Earth
items.description: Har Ki Pauri is one of the four sites of the Kumbh Mela, the largest human gathering on earth, when tens of millions come to bathe — and even on an ordinary day a guide can tell the story on the very steps where it unfolds. Context that turns a river ghat into history. The next Haridwar Kumbh falls in 2033.

items.name: Rajaji National Park (Chilla safari)
credentials: A Project Tiger reserve with one of India's largest wild elephant populations
items.description: An 820-sq-km tiger reserve of sal forest and elephant grass along the Ganga, home to Bengal tigers, one of India's largest wild elephant populations and 300-plus bird species — a private jeep safari from the Chilla gate is a genuine wilderness morning barely 20 km from Rishikesh. Elephant safaris have recently returned. The park runs mid-November to mid-June; a private jeep with a good naturalist is the way to go.

items.name: Devprayag — the birthplace of the Ganga
items.area: ~72 km up the Char Dham road
credentials: The sacred confluence where the Ganga is born — first of the Panch Prayag
items.description: The most sacred of the five prayags, where the turquoise Alaknanda and green Bhagirathi rivers crash together and are reborn as the Ganga proper — a dramatic confluence below a cliffside temple town, still largely untouristed. Stand on the sangam steps and watch two rivers become one. A rewarding day-drive up the Char Dham highway with a picnic on the way.

items.name: The gateway to the Char Dham Yatra
items.description: Rishikesh and Haridwar are the traditional starting point of the Char Dham — the Himalayan pilgrimage to Yamunotri, Gangotri, Kedarnath and Badrinath — and even without the full circuit, a curated first leg up the Alaknanda valley to Devprayag and beyond gives a taste of the sacred road. The classic Indian spiritual journey begins here. Your advisor can shape a comfortable multi-day itinerary or a single scenic day out.

items.name: A sunrise Ganga boat & morning dip
items.description: Before the town wakes, a small boat drifts you across still, mist-hung water while pilgrims take their dawn dip and temple bells start up on both banks — the Ganga at its most peaceful, a world away from the raft crowds. The quietest, most contemplative hour on the river. A private boatman and a warm shawl make it perfect for elders.

items.name: An Ayurvedic consultation & panchakarma
items.description: Beyond the yoga, Rishikesh is a serious Ayurveda destination — a proper doctor's consultation, a personalised regimen and a course of oil therapies or gentle panchakarma cleansing, from the world-class at Ananda to focused ashram clinics. Restorative in a way a spa day is not. Your advisor matches the depth of programme to how much time you have.

items.name: Kirtan & satsang evenings
items.description: As the aarti ends, the ashrams fill with kirtan — call-and-response devotional singing that builds for hours — and satsang, quiet talks with resident teachers. Sitting in on an evening of music and stillness is the most authentic, least touristed thing you can do in Rishikesh. A guide knows which sessions welcome visitors on any given night.

items.name: Gita Bhawan & the old-town bazaars
items.description: Gita Bhawan is a vast free pilgrim complex with a scripture library, riverfront steps and stalls of Ayurvedic remedies, rudraksha malas and Ganga-jal bottles — the shopping-and-scripture heart of pilgrim Rishikesh. A colourful, grounding wander for souvenirs with meaning. Best in the cool of the early evening.

items.name: The Ganga at Muni Ki Reti (river ghats)
items.description: The stretch of clean, swimmable Ganga between the bridges where locals and pilgrims take a holy dip on white-sand shallows, the water cold and glass-clear straight off the mountains. Even a barefoot paddle at the ghats is part of the pilgrimage. Mornings are calmest; a guide points you to the safe, gentle entries for a family.

items.name: A silent meditation retreat
items.description: For those who want more than a class, Rishikesh's ashrams run structured silent retreats — days of guided meditation, pranayama and stillness with no phone and no talking — the deepest form of what draws seekers here. Transformative even in a compressed few days. Your advisor arranges the right ashram, comfort level and teacher for a first retreat.

items.name: The Maa Chandi Devi & Neel Dhara Pakshi Vihar
items.description: Below the Chandi Devi hill, the Neel Dhara bird sanctuary on a Ganga barrage draws large flocks of migratory waterbirds in winter — an unexpected, tranquil counterpoint to Haridwar's intensity, and a treat for grandparents and birdwatchers. Come in the cool early morning with binoculars. Easily paired with the temple ropeways.

items.name: Evening at the Triveni Ghat feeding & floating diyas
items.description: Beyond the aarti itself, dusk at Triveni Ghat is a gentle ritual — feeding the sacred fish in the shallows and setting a leaf-boat lamp adrift on the current with a wish, a quiet moment even small children love. A soft, personal counterpart to the grand ceremonies. Buy a diya from the ghat stalls as the light fades.

items.name: Ananda in the Himalayas — cuisine
credentials: Dining within India's most awarded destination spa
Menus overseen by in-house Ayurvedic doctors and nutritionists
Repeat Condé Nast Traveller World's Best Destination Spa standing
items.description: Wellness cuisine at its most considered — Ayurvedic and calorie-conscious menus built around your programme, without ever feeling like a compromise.

items.name: Chidya Ghar, The Roseate Ganges
credentials: Signature restaurant of The Roseate Ganges (Sleeper-featured design)
Rare fine-dining focus on Kumaon/Garhwal hill cuisine
Roasted by Roseate patisserie on the same property
items.description: The city's most refined dinner — authentic Kumaon and Garhwal hill cuisine, millets and mountain produce, in a beautiful old-India room.

items.name: Riverside, Taj Rishikesh
credentials: Signature restaurant of Taj Rishikesh Resort & Spa
Focus on the food of the Himalayan states
items.description: Himalayan home cooking done properly — Kashmiri, Himachali, Garhwali, Kumaoni and Nepali classics, with the Ganges below.

items.name: The Sitting Elephant, EllBee Ganga View
credentials: Rooftop restaurant of the EllBee Ganga View boutique hotel
Panoramic Ganga and Triveni Ghat views
items.description: A rooftop table over the Ganga at Triveni Ghat — multi-cuisine vegetarian cooking with the best old-town river view in Rishikesh.

items.name: Little Buddha Café
credentials: Consistently ranked among the city's best cafés (Tripadvisor / Tripoto)
Celebrated riverside rooftop views by Laxman Jhula
items.description: Rishikesh's most-loved café — a quirky treehouse of rooftop tables over the Ganga, a fixture of the town's traveller culture since 2007.

items.name: Bistro Nirvana
credentials: A recognised Rishikesh café (Tripoto / Himalayan Yoga Association)
Noted for well-executed international vegetarian dishes
items.description: The town's most polished café cooking — well-made Continental, Indian and Middle Eastern plates a notch above the traveller-café norm.

items.name: Chotiwala
credentials: A recognised old-town institution near Ram Jhula / Swarg Ashram
items.description: A Rishikesh institution of decades — thali-style pure-vegetarian cooking that still pulls pilgrims and locals to the old town.

items.name: The Ganga Aarti — the evening ritual
credentials: Rishikesh is a legally DRY, strictly vegetarian holy city — no public bars or alcohol sale
The dusk Ganga Aarti is the defining evening
Held nightly at Triveni Ghat and Parmarth Niketan
items.description: Rishikesh's real 'night out' is spiritual, not spirited — the sunset aarti on the ghats is where the whole city gathers after dark.

items.name: Riverside cafés & bonfire evenings
credentials: Alcohol-free rooftop cafés over the Ganga (Little Buddha, Bistro Nirvana and others)
Bonfire evenings at riverside camps toward Shivpuri
No alcohol served — chai, coffee and conversation
items.description: After the aarti, the town winds down over chai, cold coffee and a Ganga-side rooftop — or a bonfire at a riverside camp upstream.

items.title: Private wellness residency at a Himalayan-foothills retreat
items.description: A tailored programme of yoga, Ayurveda and consultation at a serious ashram-style resort above the river.

items.title: Private Ganga aarti by the river at Parmarth or Triveni
items.description: The evening fire ceremony on the banks, arranged with a quiet vantage away from the main crowd.

items.title: Dawn white-water descent of the upper Ganga
items.description: An early guided rafting run through the gorges when the water and light are at their best (open season only).

items.title: Sunrise Himalayan trek or Kunjapuri viewpoint drive
items.description: An early ascent to a ridge temple for the first light over the snow peaks.

plan.heading: 3 days in Rishikesh, done well
plan.lede: A day-by-day shape for the trip — the pace we would set. Your advisor books the flights and the rooms; the days are yours.

slots.label: Morning
slots.text: Settle into a suite at Ananda in the Himalayas on the Maharaja of Tehri-Garhwal's palace estate, and take the medical consultation that sets your programme for the stay.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.text: A quiet Abhyanga treatment at the Ananda spa, then time on the palace lawns above the Ganga valley as the light softens.

slots.label: Evening
slots.text: Dinner at Ananda's restaurant with a river-valley view, ordering from the sattvic side of the menu.

days.title: The old town and the ghats

slots.label: Morning
slots.text: Drive down to Ram Jhula and walk the quieter Parmarth Niketan side, then a private hatha session on the ghat before the crowds.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.text: Cross to the Triveni Ghat area with a guide who knows the sadhu lineages, and see the Beatles Ashram (Chaurasi Kutia) walls and their murals in the afternoon calm.

slots.label: Evening
slots.text: Arrive early for the Ganga Aarti at Parmarth Niketan, seated at the front, then a light supper back at the retreat.

slots.label: Morning
slots.text: An early guided rafting stretch on the upper Ganga from Shivpuri, run gently rather than for thrills, with a riverside breakfast after.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.text: A short forest walk toward the Neer Garh waterfall, then back for a closing spa treatment.

slots.label: Evening
slots.text: A private vegetarian thali dinner on the terrace, watching the last light on the far ridge.

cta.label: Have your advisor arrange the stay

items.name: Upstream / far bank (near Laxman Jhula and beyond)
items.description: Quieter, greener and retreat-oriented; best for wellness and calm.

items.name: Tapovan
items.description: The yoga-school and cafe cluster; suits longer-stay practitioners and the young crowd.

items.name: Riverside resort belt (towards Shivpuri)
items.description: Where the adventure camps and higher-end riverside stays sit; for rafting and river life.

events.name: International Yoga Festival
events.note: A week of teachers and practitioners from around the world at Parmarth Niketan, the town's signature gathering.

events.name: Ganga Dussehra
events.note: A river festival honouring the descent of the Ganga, with special aartis and bathing on the ghats.

events.name: Kartik Purnima / Ganga aarti season
events.note: The cool-season full moon brings especially devout riverside ceremonies.

events.name: Shivratri
events.note: A significant night for this Shiva-associated pilgrimage town, with all-night devotion.

onGround.heading: On the ground

rows.label: Arriving
rows.value: Fly into Dehradun's Jolly Grant Airport (DED), roughly an hour's chauffeured drive to Rishikesh; from Delhi, a private helicopter charter to Dehradun shortens the journey considerably.

rows.label: Getting around
rows.value: A private car with driver for the temple town and the outlying ashram belt, and unhurried walking along the Ganga ghats and the two suspension bridges, which are closed to cars.

rows.label: Connectivity
rows.value: Airtel and Jio 4G/5G hold well in town; buy a local SIM at Delhi or Dehradun airport, as most eSIMs for foreign passports do not apply to Indian travellers here.

rows.label: Money
rows.value: Indian rupee; cards work at hotels and better cafés but keep cash for riverside markets, temples and river guides; a small tip for drivers and boatmen is customary.

onGround.note: Rishikesh is a sattvic town, so much of it is vegetarian and alcohol-free; dress modestly at the ghats and temples, and stay on the quieter Tapovan or Neelkanth side for calm above the day-tripper crowds.

rows.label: Climate
rows.value: October to April is kind, with clear days and cool nights; avoid May-June, when the plains heat climbs past 40C, and July-August, when the monsoon brings landslides and closes the rafting.

rows.label: Flights from India
rows.value: No airport in Rishikesh; fly to Dehradun (Jolly Grant, DED), a 45-minute drive away. Direct from Delhi (about 55 min, IndiGo/Air India) and Mumbai (via Delhi, about 3 hrs total). No lounge worth the wait at DED, so use the flagship lounge at your Delhi/Mumbai origin and keep the connection tight.

rows.label: Health & safety
rows.value: No special vaccinations beyond routine; carry standard Hepatitis A/Typhoid cover. Safe and calm town; the Ganga current is strong, so swim only where guided. Drink sealed or filtered water only.

rows.label: Dining, veg & Jain
rows.value: Effortless: Rishikesh is a pilgrimage town and largely vegetarian, with no meat, alcohol, or eggs served in the temple belt. Jain food is widely understood. Chotiwala and the cafes above Laxman Jhula do reliable, clean vegetarian fare.

collections.lede: Every place we send you appears here on merit — follow the thread to more like it.

closing.headingHtml: Rishikesh, with someone who knows it.
closing.lede: Your advisor arranges the flights, the rooms and the visa — the trip, handled.

seo.title: Rome — TripAgent
seo.description: Rome, in hand: where to stay, what to do, where to eat and where the night goes — the addresses worth knowing.

hero.name: Rome
hero.tagline: The Eternal City, layered in empire, faith and dolce vita.

ourTake.lede: Rome rewards early mornings and long dinners; the Vatican and the Colosseum are yours only before nine or after five, so book the first slot and lunch late like a Roman. Don't try to see it all, stand in one great space, a piazza, a single church, and let it work rather than sprinting between checklists. Skip the restaurants ringing the monuments entirely; walk ten minutes into Trastevere or Monti and eat where the tables are Roman.
ourTake.comeIf: You want to walk through three thousand years of art, ruins and living street life, then eat exceptionally well every night.
ourTake.skipIf: You are chasing beaches, wilderness or a quiet resort escape with no crowds.
