credentials: Condé Nast Traveller Readers' Choice 2025 — Favourite Hotel for Weddings in India
items.description: A private-island palace of its own — a serene, self-contained world twenty minutes from the old city.

items.name: RAAS Devigarh
credentials: Condé Nast Traveller — Hot List & Gold List
World Travel Awards 2024 — India's Leading Palace Hotel
items.description: An 18th-century hill fort turned pared-back, all-suite retreat — heritage stripped to serene white stone.

items.name: Taj Fateh Prakash Palace
credentials: Condé Nast Traveller Readers' Travel Awards 2024 — Taj Hotels honoured
Condé Nast Traveler — Udaipur luxury hotels list (2024)
items.description: A working wing of the Maharana's own City Palace — crystal galleries, courtyards and lake views within the walls.

items.name: Taj Aravali Resort & Spa
credentials: World Travel Awards 2025 — India's Leading Resort & Rajasthan's Leading Resort
World Travel Awards 2024 — Rajasthan's Leading Resort
items.description: A hill-country resort spread over 27 acres — the Aravallis for a view, and a serious spa at its heart.

items.name: Fateh Garh
credentials: Condé Nast Traveller — Six Sexiest Pools in the World
items.description: A reassembled Rajput haveli on a hilltop, looking down over the lakes and the City Palace.

items.name: Trident Udaipur
credentials: Travel + Leisure India's Best Awards 2024 — Best Five-Star Family Hotel/Resort in India
items.description: The Oberoi group's dependable, well-run house in mango groves beside the lake — polish without the icon's price.

items.name: Bujera Fort
credentials: Condé Nast Traveler — Udaipur luxury hotels list (2024, recommended)
items.description: A small, personally-run fort-house of real character, with the lakes and Monsoon Palace laid out below.

items.name: City Palace of Udaipur
items.description: The living seat of the Mewar dynasty, the oldest ruling family in the world, rising in tiers of balconies and mirror-work above Lake Pichola. Come early with a palace historian; the private royal apartments and the Zenana Mahal reward a slow, unhurried morning far more than a rushed group tour.

items.name: Crystal Gallery
items.description: Maharana Sajjan Singh's untouched 1877 order of Birmingham crystal, so vast it was never fully unpacked in his lifetime, including crystal chairs, tables, fountains and even a jewelled bed. A hushed, one-of-a-kind room that rewards the collector's eye; pair it with a look down into the gilded Durbar Hall.

items.name: Sunset boat ride on Lake Pichola
items.description: The essential Udaipur hour: a boat gliding past the Taj Lake Palace and the ghats as the Aravallis turn rose and gold behind them. A privately chartered boat from the City Palace jetty at golden hour, arranged through your hotel, turns a shared cruise into your own royal romance on the water.

items.name: Jag Mandir island palace
items.description: The 17th-century island pleasure-palace of black-and-white marble that sheltered Prince Khurram, later Shah Jahan, and is said to have inspired the Taj Mahal. Step off the boat for a candle-lit dinner under the domed Gul Mahal, a favourite setting for intimate royal-style celebrations and proposals.

items.name: Taj Lake Palace
items.description: The white-marble palace that seems to float on Lake Pichola, built by Maharana Jagat Singh II and now one of the most romantic hotels on earth, reached only by the hotel's own boat. Even non-residents can arrange a lunch or high tea by boat; for a stay, it is the definitive multi-generational Udaipur address.

items.name: Jagdish Temple
items.description: A soaring 1651 Indo-Aryan temple to Lord Vishnu, carved with elephants and musicians and alive with aarti bells a short walk from the palace gate. Slip in for the morning or evening aarti; the temple sits at the head of the old-city lanes, so it makes the natural start to a heritage walk.

items.name: Sajjangarh (Monsoon Palace) at sunset
items.description: The white hilltop palace built to watch the monsoon clouds roll in, now the finest sunset perch in Udaipur, with all three lakes and the old city laid out below. Time the drive up for late afternoon; a private car and a picnic from your hotel make the golden hour genuinely memorable.

items.name: Bagore ki Haveli & the Dharohar dance show
items.description: A restored 18th-century noble's haveli on the Pichola waterfront whose evening Dharohar show is the best folk performance in Rajasthan, ending with a dancer balancing eleven brass pots on her head. Book the front row; the courtyard setting under lamplight is intimate and family-friendly across generations.

items.name: Fateh Sagar Lake & Nehru Garden
items.description: The city's second great lake, ringed by the Aravallis, with a little island garden reached by boat and a breezy promenade that locals stroll at dusk. A gentle counterpoint to the palace crowds; the lakeside cafes and the sunset light make it an easy, unhurried outing for families.

items.name: Saheliyon ki Bari
items.description: The Garden of the Maidens, laid out by Maharana Sangram Singh for the royal ladies, with lotus pools, marble elephants and fountains that run on nothing but gravity from the lake above. A cool, shaded, thoroughly photogenic hour; children love the elephant fountains that switch on for visitors.

items.name: Ambrai Ghat
items.area: Hanuman Ghat, west bank of Lake Pichola
items.description: The single best face-on view of the City Palace and Lake Palace, especially when both light up at night and mirror in the water. Come for a sundowner at the ghat-side terrace; it is the postcard of Udaipur and the reason the west bank is worth crossing to.

items.name: Gangaur Ghat
items.description: The most atmospheric of Pichola's stepped ghats, framed by the triple-arched Tripolia gateway and busiest during the spring Gangaur festival, when the lake fills with lamp-lit processions. Wander down at dawn to watch the old city wake by the water before the day's boats set out.

items.name: Bada Bazaar & the old city lanes
items.description: The warren of lanes between Jagdish Temple and Clock Tower, where generations of families still sell silver, block-printed textiles, bangles and Mewari miniatures from tiny shophouses. Best explored on foot with a guide who knows the genuine ateliers; a discreet private tailor or silversmith visit can be arranged.

items.name: Miniature painting workshop
items.description: Udaipur is the living heart of the Mewar school of miniature painting, and the old-city ateliers still work in squirrel-hair brushes and stone-ground pigments as they did for the Maharanas. A private session with a master painter, watching a peacock or a Krishna scene emerge on marble or old paper, is a quietly extraordinary keepsake.

items.name: Vintage & Classic Car Collection
items.description: The Mewar royal garage, with the 1934 Rolls-Royce Phantom and Cadillac convertibles that carried Maharanas and Queen Elizabeth II, kept in the original 1930s state motor house. A short, delightful stop for car lovers and multi-gen families; several of the cars still run for palace weddings.

items.name: Shilpgram crafts village
items.area: West of Fateh Sagar, near Havala village
items.description: A living rural-arts complex where potters, weavers, puppeteers and painters from across western India work in recreated village huts, most vivid during the winter Shilpgram Utsav. A relaxed way to meet artisans and buy at the source; a good half-day for families with children.

items.name: Ahar cenotaphs & museum
items.area: Ahar, 2 km east of the city
items.description: A serene field of some nineteen royal cenotaphs where the Maharanas of Mewar were cremated, beside a small museum holding pottery and a rare 10th-century Buddha and finds dating back nearly four thousand years. Almost always empty, it is a soulful, contemplative counterweight to the palaces.

items.name: Karni Mata ropeway to Machla Magra
items.description: A short cable-car glide up Machla Magra hill to the Karni Mata temple, delivering a sweeping bird's-eye of Lake Pichola, the City Palace and the old city at your feet. Ride up near sunset; it pairs neatly with the Doodh Talai gardens and musical fountain below.

items.name: Doodh Talai musical fountain & gardens
items.area: Doodh Talai, south of the old city
items.description: A pretty lakelet at the foot of the ropeway hill, with rock gardens, a sunset point and an evening musical fountain that draws local families. An easy, low-key evening stroll with lake views; combine it with the ropeway for a gentle end to the day.

items.name: Neemach Mata hike
items.description: A steepish climb up Dewali hill to a hilltop temple to the royal household goddess, rewarded with one of the widest, least-crowded panoramas of Fateh Sagar and the city. Go at first light for the cool and the birdlife; a genuinely local, active alternative to the driving circuit.

items.name: Badi Lake (Bari ka Talab)
items.area: Badi village, ~12 km from the city
items.description: A serene, offbeat lake built by Maharana Raj Singh I after a famine, with clean marble ghats and hills all around and far fewer visitors than the city lakes. A favourite quiet-escape picnic spot; beautiful in the monsoon when the overflow spills over the stone weirs.

items.name: Sukhadia Circle
items.description: A grand three-tiered marble fountain on a landscaped roundabout that comes alive in the evening with illuminated water and a lively food market of chaat, faluda and street snacks. A cheerful, unpretentious evening for families; the veg street food is plentiful and easy for Jain diners.

items.name: Gulab Bagh (Sajjan Niwas Garden)
items.area: Between City Palace and Lake Pichola
items.description: Udaipur's largest garden, a hundred-acre Victorian-era rose park laid out by Maharana Sajjan Singh, with a heritage library, lotus ponds and shaded avenues in the heart of the old city. A calm green lung for a morning walk; the toy train pleases younger children.

items.name: Heritage walk of the old city
items.description: A guided morning weave through the lanes from Jagdish Temple past painted havelis, silversmiths, temple courtyards and hidden Pichola viewpoints that you would never find alone. The best single introduction to Udaipur's texture; the top hotels arrange private historian-led walks tailored to your interests.

items.name: Kumbhalgarh Fort
credentials: UNESCO World Heritage Site — Kumbhalgarh Fort, part of the Hill Forts of Rajasthan
items.description: The mighty 15th-century mountain fortress of Rana Kumbha, wrapped in a defensive wall over 36 km long, second only to the Great Wall of China, birthplace of the legendary Maharana Pratap. Time the visit for the late-afternoon light on the ramparts and stay for the sound-and-light show; combine with Ranakpur in one grand day.

items.name: Ranakpur Jain temples
items.description: A 15th-century marble masterpiece to the Tirthankara Adinatha, its 1,444 pillars each carved differently so no two are alike, set in a quiet forested valley. Deeply serene and naturally Jain-reverent; usually paired with Kumbhalgarh, it is worth lingering over the marble at an unhurried pace.

items.name: Chittorgarh Fort
credentials: UNESCO World Heritage Site — Chittorgarh Fort, part of the Hill Forts of Rajasthan
items.description: The largest fort in India and the emotional heart of Rajput valour, its towers of victory and fame rising over the scene of three legendary sieges and the jauhar of Rani Padmini. A powerful, story-laden full day; a good guide brings the Vijay Stambh and Padmini's palace to life.

items.name: Nathdwara — Shrinathji Temple
items.description: The most revered Krishna shrine of the Pushtimarg tradition, where the seven-year-old Shrinathji is dressed and worshipped through eight daily darshans amid the town's famous Pichwai painters. A meaningful pilgrimage half-day; the giant hand-painted Pichwai cloths make it a magnet for collectors.

items.name: Eklingji Temple complex
items.description: The ancestral temple of Lord Shiva as ruling deity of Mewar, a complex of some 108 shrines in white marble and black stone where the Maharana still worships as the god's regent. Atmospheric and devout; go for the evening aarti and pair with Nagda next door.

items.name: Nagda — Sas-Bahu temples
items.area: Day trip, ~23 km north, near Eklingji
items.description: A pair of exquisitely carved 10th-century Vishnu temples beside a lake, their intricate stonework among the oldest and finest in the region, a short hop from Eklingji. A tranquil, uncrowded stop for lovers of ancient temple architecture; easily folded into the Eklingji-Nathdwara circuit.

items.name: Jaisamand Lake (Dhebar Lake)
items.description: One of Asia's largest artificial lakes, dammed in 1685 by Maharana Jai Singh, with marble cenotaphs, summer palaces and islands, and a wildlife sanctuary on its hilly shores. A wide, wild-feeling escape from the city bustle; boating and birdlife make it a rewarding leisurely day.

items.name: Menar bird village
items.description: A community-protected 'bird village' whose lakes host thousands of migratory birds each winter, from flamingos to cranes, watched over by villagers who guard rather than hunt them. A soulful dawn outing for birders and photographers; best from November to February.

items.name: The Oberoi Udaivilas grounds
items.area: Haridasji ki Magri, west bank of Lake Pichola
items.description: A palace-hotel of gilded domes, reflecting pools and its own stretch of Pichola shoreline, consistently rated among the world's finest resorts and set within a wildlife-rich former royal hunting reserve. Even for non-residents, a private boat arrival for lunch or spa is a serene indulgence; for a stay it is Udaipur luxury at its peak.

items.name: Sunset at Ambrai / Lake Pichola dinner cruise
items.description: As the palaces light up, a slow private boat with a Mewari thali or a chef's tasting on board turns dinner into the definitive Udaipur evening. Easily arranged through heritage hotels, with veg and Jain menus as the effortless default; a favourite for anniversaries and quiet family celebrations.

items.name: Rajasthani cooking class
items.description: Learn dal-baati-churma, gatte ki sabzi and Mewari sweets from a home cook in an old-city haveli kitchen, often ending with a rooftop meal over the lake. Naturally vegetarian and Jain-adaptable, it is a warm, hands-on way for families to take a taste of Udaipur home.

items.name: Miniature-painting shopping at the source
items.description: Beyond a workshop, the serious Mewar-miniature galleries near Jagdish Temple sell museum-grade work on old paper, silk and marble, some by nationally recognised master families. A discreet, guided visit lets collectors commission or acquire genuine pieces rather than tourist reproductions.

items.name: Silver & textile shopping in the old city
items.description: Udaipur's lanes are a treasury of tribal silver, bandhani and block-printed textiles, and Rajasthani jootis, sold by families who have traded here for generations. A knowledgeable guide steers you to the authentic ateliers; bespoke tailoring and private silver appointments can be set up through your hotel.

items.name: Vintage-car heritage drive
items.description: The royal household still runs some of its vintage Rolls-Royces and Cadillacs for special occasions, and a chauffeured heritage-car drive to a palace dinner is a signature Mewar flourish. A memorable touch for weddings and milestone celebrations, arranged through the palace's own hospitality group.

items.name: Vidhya Niwas / rooftop lake-view sundowners
items.description: The old-city rooftops on Lal Ghat and Hanuman Ghat look straight across Pichola to the palaces, and a sundowner up top is the local way to end a day of walking. Choose a quiet heritage rooftop rather than the crowded cafes for the calmest, most cinematic view.

items.name: Haldighati battlefield & Maharana Pratap memorial
items.area: Day trip, ~40 km north, near Nathdwara
items.description: The narrow mountain pass where Maharana Pratap and his beloved horse Chetak fought the Mughals in 1576, now with a museum and memorial that tell the Mewar valour story vividly. A short, stirring add-on to the Eklingji-Nathdwara circuit, especially with children learning the legend.

items.name: Sunset point & rope-walk at Machla Magra
items.description: The landscaped sunset garden atop Machla Magra hill offers a calm, ticketed viewpoint over the lakes without the crowds of Sajjangarh. A quieter in-city sunset option that pairs perfectly with the Karni Mata ropeway ride up.

items.name: Bohra Ganesh Temple
items.description: A much-loved local Ganesh temple, one of the oldest in the city, thronged by students and families seeking blessings, especially before exams and new ventures. A gentle, genuinely local devotional stop away from the tourist trail, best in the morning.

items.name: Vintage boat to Mohan Mandir & Arsi Vilas
items.description: Beyond Jag Mandir, Pichola holds the small royal island pavilions of Mohan Mandir and the bird-rich Arsi Vilas islet, seen on a longer private boat loop. A quieter, connoisseur's angle on the lake for those who want more than the standard cruise.

items.name: Spa & wellness at a palace hotel
items.description: Udaipur's palace resorts offer some of India's finest spas, from Ayurvedic royal rituals to lake-view treatment pavilions and yoga at dawn over the water. A restorative anchor to a multi-generational stay, easily woven around the sightseeing days.

items.name: Kumbhalgarh Wildlife Sanctuary trek
items.area: Day trip / overnight, Aravalli hills near Kumbhalgarh
items.description: The forested hills around the great fort protect leopards, wolves and sloth bears, with guided nature walks and jeep trails through wild Aravalli country. A rugged, active add-on for those extending the Kumbhalgarh day into an overnight in the hills.

items.name: Sheesh Mahal
credentials: Inside Taj Lake Palace — Tripadvisor Travellers' Choice Best of the Best 2025, No. 1 One-of-a-Kind Hotel globally
items.description: Royal Mewari fine dining inside the floating palace — the grandest dinner in the city, on the water.

items.name: Udai Kothi rooftop / Sheesh Mahal restaurants in-hotel
items.area: Lake Pichola (west bank — The Oberoi Udaivilas)
credentials: Inside The Oberoi Udaivilas — Travel + Leisure World's Best Awards 2024, Best Luxury Resort (Editor's Choice, India)
items.description: Considered Indian and European cooking in the most decorated hotel in Udaipur — flawless, and framed by the lake.

items.name: Ambrai
credentials: Condé Nast Traveller India — featured Udaipur restaurant
items.description: The lakeside table with the postcard view — the City Palace and Lake Palace lit up across the water.

items.name: Upré by 1559 AD
credentials: Condé Nast Traveller India — featured Udaipur restaurant
items.description: A rooftop terrace looking straight across to the City Palace and the floating Lake Palace.

items.name: 1559 AD
credentials: Condé Nast Traveller India — featured Udaipur restaurant
items.description: Art-nouveau rooms and courtyards in a 95-year-old house, with classical live music through dinner.

items.name: Jheel's Ginger Coffee Bar & Bakery
credentials: Condé Nast Traveller India — featured Udaipur spot
items.description: A little terrace café right on the water — coffee, cake and the finest slow morning in Udaipur.

items.name: Amrit Sagar Bar
items.area: Old City / City Palace (Taj Fateh Prakash Palace)
credentials: Inside Taj Fateh Prakash Palace — Condé Nast Traveller Readers' Travel Awards 2024 (Taj Hotels honoured)
items.description: A drink among royal portraits and crystal inside the City Palace walls — the grandest nightcap in Udaipur.

items.title: Private dinner on a Lake Pichola island terrace
items.description: A candlelit table at Jag Mandir or a private jetty, with the City Palace lit gold across the water.

items.title: Vintage-car drive from the royal Mewar collection
items.description: Out through the old city and up to the Monsoon Palace in one of the Maharana's restored classic cars.

items.title: Private curator-led visit to the City Palace and its zenana
items.description: The private courtyards, miniatures and armoury of the Mewar dynasty, opened beyond the public route.

items.title: Dawn boat on Lake Pichola before the ghats wake
items.description: A quiet row past Jag Niwas and the bathing ghats in the first light, when the water is still as glass.

plan.heading: 3 days in Udaipur, done well
plan.lede: A day-by-day shape for the trip — the pace we would set. Your advisor books the flights and the rooms; the days are yours.

days.title: The lake at its own pace

slots.label: Morning
slots.text: Settle into the Taj Lake Palace or the Leela Palace, then take a private boat across Pichola to Jag Mandir before the light hardens.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.text: Walk the City Palace with a curator, lingering in the Sheesh Mahal and the Zenana courtyards rather than rushing the full circuit.

slots.label: Evening
slots.text: Sundowners on the Leela's lakefront terrace, then dinner at Sheesh Mahal at the Fateh Prakash overlooking the water.

slots.label: Morning
slots.text: A morning with a miniature painter in the old city, followed by the stepwells and the restored havelis around Bagore-ki-Haveli.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.text: Drive out to the Jagdish Temple lanes for textiles, then rest through the afternoon heat by the pool.

slots.label: Evening
slots.text: A private thali dinner at Ambrai on the ghats, with the City Palace lit across the lake.

slots.label: Morning
slots.text: Early drive to the Jain temples at Ranakpur, timed for the marble before the crowds.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.text: Lunch and a slow return via Kumbhalgarh's fort walls, or a spa afternoon back at the hotel if you'd rather stay close.

slots.label: Evening
slots.text: A last dinner at Upre by 1559 AD on the rooftop, watching the boats settle for the night.

cta.label: Have your advisor arrange the stay

items.name: Lake Pichola waterfront (Gangaur Ghat)
items.description: The old-city ghats and heritage havelis right on the water — atmospheric and walkable, best for first-timers.

items.name: Lake Palace / island stays
items.description: The famous island hotels reached only by boat; for a cocooned, once-in-a-lifetime stay cut off from the town.

items.name: Fateh Sagar & the ridge
items.description: Quieter lake and hillside above the bustle, with space and views; suits those who want calm over old-city immediacy.

events.name: Mewar Festival
events.note: A spring festival tied to Gangaur, with a Lake Pichola boat procession and City Palace celebrations honouring the goddess.

events.name: Shilpgram Utsav
events.note: The big crafts-and-folk fair at the Shilpgram rural arts village, drawing artisans from across western India.

events.name: Udaipur World Music Festival
events.note: A weekend of international and Indian acts across lakeside and heritage stages in the City of Lakes.

onGround.heading: On the ground

rows.label: Arriving
rows.value: Fly into Maharana Pratap Airport (UDR) at Dabok, roughly 40 minutes from the lake, and let a chauffeured car meet you airside; the Taj and Oberoi properties also arrange a private boat transfer across Lake Pichola for their island palaces.

rows.label: Getting around
rows.value: A private car with driver for the town and its temples, and a hotel boat for the lake and the island palaces — the old city itself is best seen slowly on foot.

rows.label: Connectivity
rows.value: 4G is reliable across the city and hotel wifi is strong; an Airtel or Jio eSIM loaded before arrival saves the paperwork of a local SIM.

rows.label: Money
rows.value: Indian rupee (INR); cards are accepted at hotels and better shops but keep cash for markets and boatmen, and tip around 10 percent or leave it to your hotel to settle.

onGround.note: Stay lakeside for the sunset views — the palace hotels on and around Lake Pichola are the reason to come. Dress is relaxed but cover shoulders and knees for the City Palace and Jagdish Temple, and shoes come off at temple thresholds.

rows.label: Climate
rows.value: October to March is kind: cool, clear, the lakes full after the monsoon. Avoid April to June, when the Rajasthan heat climbs past 40C, and July to September, when the rains arrive.

rows.label: Flights from India
rows.value: Direct from Delhi (approx 1h20m), Mumbai (approx 1h30m) and Bengaluru (approx 2h15m) into Maharana Pratap Airport (UDR); IndiGo and Air India run the routes, with SpiceJet on some. A small airport with a short indoor walk, so a car-to-door pickup matters more than a lounge; the hotels send one.

rows.label: Health & safety
rows.value: No vaccinations required beyond routine cover; carry the usual Hep A/typhoid boosters if not current. Very safe, calm city. Drink sealed or filtered water only, as everywhere in India.

rows.label: Dining, veg & Jain
rows.value: Effortless for vegetarian and Jain travellers; Rajasthani cuisine is largely vegetarian and Jain (no onion/garlic) versions are understood everywhere. Ambrai and the hotel dining rooms at the Oberoi Udaivilas and Taj Lake Palace do refined vegetarian thalis.

seo.title: Vancouver — TripAgent
seo.description: Vancouver, in hand: where to stay, what to do, where to eat and where the night goes — the addresses worth knowing.

hero.name: Vancouver
hero.tagline: Mountains, sea and rainforest framing a glass city.

ourTake.lede: Vancouver rewards the traveller who treats the city as a base rather than the destination — the mountains, the ocean and the islands are where it comes alive. Give downtown a night or two, then point yourself at Stanley Park, the North Shore and the water. Skip the aquarium-and-Gastown-clock circuit; spend that time on Granville Island early, before the tour groups.
ourTake.comeIf: You want mountains, ocean and forest at the edge of a relaxed city, with Whistler close by.
ourTake.skipIf: You want guaranteed sun outside summer or a fast, urban-only break.

whenToGo.blurb: Come June to September for dry, glorious days on ocean and mountain; time spring for cherry blossom and whale season, and expect grey rain the rest of the year.
whenToGo.bestMonths: May, Jun, Jul, Aug and Sep

guide.lede: Where to stay, what to do, where to eat, and where the night goes — grouped by price, every address earned by a name worth trusting.

items.name: Fairmont Pacific Rim
credentials: Forbes Travel Guide Five-Star (2025) — hotel and spa
items.description: Vancouver's defining modern grand hotel — glass and art above the harbour, faced to the sea and the mountains beyond.

items.name: Rosewood Hotel Georgia
items.description: A restored 1927 landmark of old-Hollywood glamour — dark wood, a saltwater infinity pool, and the city's most storied address.

items.name: Shangri-La Vancouver
items.description: The city's tallest tower turned discreet luxury house — spacious rooms, Asian calm, MO-standard service.

items.name: Wedgewood Hotel & Spa
items.description: A family-owned European jewel on Robson Square — antiques, Persian rugs, and Vancouver's most personal service.

items.name: Loden Hotel
items.description: A polished boutique hideaway on the quiet edge of Coal Harbour — mid-century calm with harbour and mountain light.

items.name: The Douglas, Autograph Collection
items.description: A design-led tower rising from the Parq entertainment complex — warm cedar, mountain views, and a private urban garden.

items.name: Fairmont Hotel Vancouver
items.description: The green-roofed 'Castle in the City' since 1939 — a chateau-style landmark at the heart of downtown.

items.name: Pan Pacific Vancouver
credentials: Condé Nast Traveller Readers' Choice Awards 2025 (Best Hotels in Canada)
items.description: Perched over Canada Place under the white sails — the definitive harbour-front address, ships and seaplanes at the door.

items.name: JW Marriott Parq Vancouver
items.description: The polished flagship of the Parq complex — contemporary rooms above a rooftop park and a cluster of restaurants.

items.name: Stanley Park Seawall
items.description: A 9-kilometre paved rim traces the peninsula between old-growth forest and the sea, past the Lions Gate Bridge, English Bay and the downtown skyline. Have your guide arrange a private cycle or a slow morning stroll before the crowds; grandparents and children keep the same flat, car-free path.

items.name: Brockton Point Totem Poles
items.description: Nine towering First Nations poles stand in a meadow near the water, some carved as early as the 1880s and among the most-photographed sights in British Columbia. A small interpretive centre explains the Kwakwaka'wakw and Haida stories behind them, a gentle first read on Indigenous culture for a multi-generation group.

items.name: Prospect Point
items.description: The high bluff at the park's north tip looks straight onto the Lions Gate Bridge and the Burrard Inlet, with a cafe and gift shop for a pause. It is the classic photo-stop on a private drive around the park.

items.name: Vancouver Aquarium
items.description: Set inside Stanley Park, Canada's largest aquarium runs sea otters, jellies and a rainforest gallery that reliably holds young children for hours. A calm, indoor option when the coast turns grey.

items.name: Lost Lagoon
items.description: A tranquil freshwater lake at the park's edge, ringed by a level trail where herons and swans gather at dusk. A quiet, unhurried loop for grandparents who want the park without the full seawall.

items.name: Granville Island Public Market
items.description: An indoor food hall under the Granville Bridge where farm stalls, Oyama Sausage, Benton Brothers cheese and Belgian chocolatiers sit beside fresh-off-the-boat seafood. A private tasting walk here is the easiest, most delicious hour in the city, with plenty for vegetarians.

items.name: Granville Island artisan studios & galleries
items.description: Beyond the market, the island's converted warehouses hold glass-blowers, potters, a sake maker and independent galleries. A relaxed browse for a collector, walkable and free of traffic.

items.name: Capilano Suspension Bridge Park
items.description: A 137-metre cable bridge sways 70 metres above the Capilano River canyon, with a Treetops walk strung between 1,300-year-old Douglas firs and a glass Cliffwalk cantilevered off the rock. The engineered thrill everyone photographs; a private driver spares you the North Shore parking scrum.

items.name: Grouse Mountain
credentials: Eye of the Wind — a glass viewing pod set just below the blades of a working wind turbine, billed as the only one of its kind.
items.description: The Skyride gondola climbs to an alpine playground with 360-degree city and ocean views, a resident pair of grizzlies named Grinder and Coola, a lumberjack show and the Eye of the Wind turbine you can stand beneath. A single mountain that fills a whole family day, dawn to dusk.

items.name: Lynn Canyon Park & Suspension Bridge
items.description: A free 50-metre suspension bridge over a rainforest gorge with waterfalls and swimming holes, the local's quieter answer to Capilano. Bring a private guide and you get temperate rainforest with none of the ticket-gate crowds.

items.name: Gastown & the Steam Clock
items.description: Vancouver's oldest quarter, all cobblestones and Victorian brick, anchored by the whistling steam clock that puffs Westminster chimes on the quarter-hour. Boutiques, First Nations galleries and some of the city's best restaurants line the same few blocks.

items.name: Chinatown
items.description: One of North America's largest historic Chinatowns, with the ornate Millennium Gate, herbalists and a growing wave of new restaurants and bars. Best explored on foot with a guide who can read the layers of old and new.

items.name: Dr. Sun Yat-Sen Classical Chinese Garden
credentials: The first authentic classical Chinese garden built outside of China, opened in 1986.
items.description: A walled Ming Dynasty scholar's garden of jade water, limestone and pavilions, the first full classical Chinese garden built outside China. A pocket of stillness in the middle of the city, marking its 40th year in 2026.

items.name: Museum of Anthropology at UBC
credentials: Home to the world's largest collection of works by Haida artist Bill Reid.
items.description: Arthur Erickson's soaring Great Hall of glass and concrete frames towering totem poles, canoes and works from Haida, Nisga'a and Coast Salish nations, reopened in 2024 after a seismic rebuild. It holds the world's largest collection of Bill Reid, including his masterwork The Raven and the First Men.

items.name: Vancouver Art Gallery
credentials: Holds the world's most important collection of Emily Carr's work.
items.description: The city's flagship gallery, beside Robson Square, holds the world's most important collection of Emily Carr, the painter of British Columbia's forests and Indigenous villages. Through 2026 it shows its largest Carr exhibition in over twenty years.

items.name: Canada Place & the waterfront
items.description: The white sail-roofed cruise pier juts into Burrard Inlet with a seawall promenade, the Canadian Trail interpretive walk and float planes taking off from the harbour. An easy, level introduction to the city's water-meets-mountains setting.

items.name: FlyOver Canada
items.description: A flight-simulator ride inside Canada Place that suspends you before a 20-metre dome screen and sweeps you coast to coast with wind, mist and scent. Eight thrilling minutes that delight children and grandparents alike, whatever the weather outside.

items.name: Science World
items.description: The mirrored geodesic dome at the head of False Creek, built for Expo 86, is a hands-on science centre with an OMNIMAX dome theatre and floors of experiments for curious kids. Its 391 lights run programmed sequences over the water every night.

items.name: English Bay Beach
items.description: The city's most beloved downtown beach, where locals gather for sunsets over the freighters and the summer fireworks. Steps from West End restaurants, an easy stroll for an evening with the family.

items.name: Kitsilano Beach
items.description: A wide sandy beach backed by lawns, tennis courts and Vancouver's landmark 137-metre saltwater pool, framed by mountain and skyline views. The heart of laid-back "Kits", ringed by good cafes and yoga-set shops.

items.name: Queen Elizabeth Park
items.description: A former rock quarry transformed into the city's most-visited park, crowning Vancouver's highest point with formal flower gardens and a panorama of downtown against the North Shore mountains. A gentle, manicured green space for a slow multi-generation afternoon.

items.name: Bloedel Conservatory
items.description: A glass dome atop Queen Elizabeth Park holding tropical, subtropical and desert zones under one roof, with free-flying parrots and koi. A warm, colourful refuge on a rainy day, small enough not to tire anyone.

items.name: VanDusen Botanical Garden
items.description: A 22-hectare garden of 7,500 plant species across sixty themed sections, with an Elizabethan hedge maze and a striking undulating-roof visitor centre. Serene and never crowded, ideal for a private morning wander.

items.name: Lonsdale Quay & the SeaBus crossing
items.description: Ride the SeaBus twelve minutes across the harbour for one of the great cheap skyline views, landing at a lively public market and the neon Shipyards district. A short, scenic outing that feels like a proper voyage to the children.

items.name: Commercial Drive
items.description: The city's old Italian quarter, now a bohemian stretch of espresso bars, patios and independent shops known simply as "The Drive". A neighbourhood to wander for anyone who wants the real, unpolished Vancouver.

items.name: Punjabi Market (Little India)
items.description: The stretch of Main Street between 49th and 51st that has been Vancouver's Little India since the 1970s, with sari shops, sweet houses and institutions like the Himalaya Restaurant. A nostalgic, homely detour for Indian families, quieter now that much of the community has moved to Surrey.

items.name: Surrey & the South Asian food belt
items.description: Home to one of the largest Punjabi communities outside India, Surrey's Newton and Payal Business Centre serve the region's most authentic Punjabi, Gujarati and South Indian cooking, plus gurdwaras and sweet shops. Worth a private car trip for a homesick, food-loving multi-gen group.

items.name: Aberdeen Centre & the Golden Village
items.description: Richmond's Golden Village is one of North America's densest concentrations of Asian malls and restaurants, with Aberdeen Centre's food court and bubble-tea culture the anchor. A vegetarian-friendly, kid-pleasing crash course in Hong Kong and Taiwanese food.

items.name: Richmond Night Market
credentials: The largest night market in North America.
items.description: The largest night market in North America, over a hundred stalls and 500-plus dishes of hawker-style Asian street food under strings of lights, running weekend evenings from spring to September. A festive, sensory night out for all ages; a private driver makes the far-out location painless.

items.name: Steveston Village
items.description: A historic fishing village where you can buy salmon and crab straight off the boats at Fisherman's Wharf, tour a heritage cannery and stroll a boardwalk to the river's mouth. A charming, low-key half-day with genuine maritime character.

items.name: Sea-to-Sky Gondola
items.description: A ten-minute climb above Howe Sound to a summit lodge with a viewing platform, a suspension bridge and alpine trails looking over turquoise fjord water. The quieter, more natural alternative to Whistler's Peak 2 Peak, an hour up the coast.

items.name: Sea-to-Sky Highway drive
items.description: One of the world's great coastal drives, hugging the Howe Sound fjord from Vancouver past Shannon Falls and Squamish up to Whistler. With a private driver it becomes a leisurely day of turnouts, waterfalls and photographs rather than a slog.

items.name: Shannon Falls
items.description: British Columbia's third-highest waterfall at 335 metres, a short flat walk from the Sea-to-Sky Highway to a viewing platform in the spray. A five-minute stop that feels like a proper wilderness moment.

items.name: Whistler Village
items.description: A pedestrian alpine resort of cobbled lanes, patios and boutiques ninety minutes north, framed by two ski mountains and buzzing summer and winter alike. The natural base for a mountain day, or an overnight for a longer stay.

items.name: Peak 2 Peak Gondola
credentials: Holds the Guinness record for highest cable car above ground, at 436 metres, and among the longest unsupported spans between two towers, at just over three kilometres.
items.description: A glass-floored gondola glides between Whistler and Blackcomb mountains, hanging 436 metres above the valley across a single record-setting span, with the Peak Suspension Bridge at the top. The showstopper mountain experience for a group out to be wowed.

items.name: Victoria & the Inner Harbour
items.description: British Columbia's genteel capital, reached by ferry or floatplane, wraps its harbour with the ivy-clad Fairmont Empress and the domed Parliament Buildings, made for afternoon tea and a slow waterfront wander. A full day, or better an overnight, paired with Butchart Gardens.

items.name: The Butchart Gardens
credentials: Designated a National Historic Site of Canada.
items.description: A 55-acre floral masterpiece near Victoria, built inside a spent limestone quarry, whose Sunken Garden is among the most celebrated garden spaces in the world. A National Historic Site, still family-owned after 120-plus years, spectacular whatever the season.

items.name: Bowen Island
items.description: A twenty-minute ferry from Horseshoe Bay lands you at Snug Cove, an artist's island of cafes, galleries, sandy coves and fifty kilometres of forest trails with no chain in sight. Vancouver's closest island escape, easy and unhurried for a half-day.

items.name: Cypress Mountain lookout
items.description: A short mountain drive above West Vancouver ends at a lookout that takes in the whole city, the Gulf Islands and, on a clear day, Mount Baker across the border. The best sunset panorama within twenty minutes of downtown.

items.name: Deep Cove
items.description: A postcard cove tucked into the fjord where you can rent a kayak on calm water, walk the Quarry Rock trail for a view, and reward the effort with a famous Honey's doughnut. A gentle, pretty morning off the tourist trail.

items.name: Nitobe Memorial Garden
items.description: A serene Japanese stroll-and-tea garden on the UBC campus, considered one of the most authentic outside Japan, with a tea house, koi and maples that blaze in autumn. A meditative counterpoint to the nearby Museum of Anthropology.

items.name: Grouse Grind trail
items.description: A relentless 2.9-kilometre staircase up the face of Grouse Mountain, known as "Mother Nature's Stairmaster", that fit visitors climb before riding the gondola back down. For the athletic member of the party who wants a real challenge with a view.

items.name: Second Beach & Ceperley Meadow
items.description: A family beach on the Stanley Park seawall with a heated outdoor pool, a playground and a big grassy meadow for a picnic. The easiest spot to let children loose while adults take in the sea view.

items.name: Vancouver Lookout at Harbour Centre
items.description: A glass elevator shoots up to a 360-degree observation deck 168 metres over downtown, taking in the harbour, Stanley Park and the mountains in one turn. The quickest way to orient a group on their first day.

items.name: Robson Street shopping
items.description: The city's flagship shopping promenade, running from the art gallery toward Stanley Park, mixing global luxury names with cafes and people-watching patios. The obvious stroll for a retail afternoon downtown.

items.name: Mount Seymour
items.description: The least-visited of the three North Shore peaks, a quieter drive up to alpine meadows, easy family trails in summer and gentle ski slopes in winter, all with a broad valley view. The insider's choice when Grouse feels too busy.

items.name: Yaletown
items.description: A former warehouse district turned polished waterfront neighbourhood of loading-dock patios, design shops and marina views onto False Creek. The stylish quarter for an evening of dinner and a stroll along the seawall.

items.name: Masayoshi
items.description: Masayoshi Baba's serene sushi counter — exacting edomae craft away from the downtown crowds.

items.name: Okeya Kyujiro
items.description: A theatrical kaiseki-and-sushi experience under lantern light — dining as performance.

items.name: Sushi Hyun
items.description: A minimalist omakase counter of great purity — fish flown in and treated with reverence.

items.name: Sushi Masuda
items.description: A Tokyo-trained master's edomae counter — classical sushi of quiet, uncompromising standard.

items.name: AnnaLena
items.description: Playful, precise contemporary cooking in a warm West-Side room — Vancouver at its most confidently modern.

items.name: Barbara
items.description: A tiny, ingredient-obsessed counter in Chinatown — a personal tasting menu of quiet intensity.

items.name: Burdock & Co
items.description: Andrea Carlson's seasonal, farm-driven cooking — Pacific Northwest terroir on a plate.

items.name: iDen & QuanJuDe Beijing Duck House
items.description: The famed Beijing duck house brought to Vancouver — lacquered Peking duck of real ceremony.

items.name: Kissa Tanto
items.description: A moody, 1960s-Tokyo-jazz-bar room serving singular Japanese-Italian cooking — one of the city's most-loved tables.

items.name: Published on Main
items.description: The city's most celebrated modern room — refined, seasonal cooking on buzzing Main Street.

items.name: St. Lawrence
items.description: A Québécois-French bistro dressed as a Montréal railway diner — hearty, exact, deeply comforting.

items.name: Sumibiyaki Arashi
items.description: An intimate charcoal-grill counter — yakitori and sumibiyaki cooked with quiet precision.

items.name: Botanist
items.description: Modern Canadian cooking inside the Fairmont Pacific Rim — polished, seasonal, and beautifully served.

items.name: Vij's
items.description: Vikram Vij's landmark of modern Indian cooking — the restaurant that reimagined Indian food in Canada.

items.name: Karma Indian Bistro
items.description: Refined, generous Indian cooking that earned Michelin's value nod — warm and familiar for Indian palates.

items.name: Anh and Chi
items.description: Beloved, beautifully run modern Vietnamese on Main — family-owned and full of heart.

items.name: Phnom Penh
items.description: The legendary Cambodian-Vietnamese room — its butter beef and chicken wings are a Vancouver rite of passage.

items.name: Fable Kitchen
items.description: Honest farm-to-table cooking on West 4th — rustic, seasonal and consistently good.

items.name: Good Thief
items.description: An inventive, value-driven room that won Michelin's newest nod on Main — bold and unexpected.

items.name: The Lunch Lady
items.description: A Vancouver homage to Saigon's famous street-food matriarch — bright, punchy Vietnamese.

items.name: 1927 Lobby Lounge, Rosewood Hotel Georgia
credentials: Inside a MICHELIN Two-Key hotel — a restored 1927 landmark
items.description: A jewel-box hotel lounge under the restored 1927 ceiling — the city's most glamorous nightcap.

items.name: Bacchus, Wedgewood Hotel & Spa
credentials: Inside a Relais & Châteaux, MICHELIN One-Key hotel
items.description: A clubby, wood-panelled piano bar in a Relais & Châteaux house — Vancouver's most European nightcap.

items.name: Botanist Bar
credentials: North America's 50 Best Bars 2025 (No. 26) — highest Vancouver entry
items.description: The bar inside Vancouver's only Forbes Five-Star hotel — botanically-driven cocktails and the city's highest-ranked drinking room.

items.name: The Keefer Bar
credentials: Named Best Bar in Canada on the 2025 list
items.description: An apothecary-themed cocktail den inspired by Chinatown's historic herbalists — dark, aromatic and thrilling.

items.name: Prophecy
credentials: North America's 50 Best Bars 2025 (No. 53, extended list)
items.description: A refined, low-lit cocktail room bringing serious drinks and hospitality to Gastown — a rising Vancouver name.

items.name: Meo
credentials: North America's 50 Best Bars 2025 (No. 92, extended list)
items.description: An inventive, intimate cocktail bar with a devoted following — one of the city's newest 50-Best names.

items.name: Reflections, The Rooftop, The Douglas
credentials: Inside a MICHELIN Guide selected hotel — a seasonal urban-garden rooftop
items.description: A garden terrace above the Parq complex — fire pits, greenery and open-air drinks over the city.

items.name: Laowai
credentials: North America's 50 Best Bars 2025 (No. 67, extended list)
Named Best New Bar in Canada (2022)
items.description: A hidden 1920s-Shanghai speakeasy behind a freezer door — velvet, brass and glamour, and drinks to match.

items.title: Seaplane to a Gulf Island lunch
items.description: A harbour floatplane lifts off downtown and sets you down for the afternoon on Salt Spring or Pender.

items.title: Heli-skiing day out of Whistler
items.description: A short transfer north puts you on untracked coastal-range powder with a private guide and no lift lines.

items.title: Sunset dinner in Stanley Park
items.description: Book the seawall-facing tables so the light off Burrard Inlet does the work.

items.title: Private sailing charter of Howe Sound
items.description: A skippered day among the fjords and islets, often with harbour seals and eagles for company.

plan.heading: 3 days in Vancouver, done well
plan.lede: A day-by-day shape for the trip — the pace we would set. Your advisor books the flights and the rooms; the days are yours.

slots.label: Morning
slots.text: Settle into the Fairmont Pacific Rim, then cycle or walk the Stanley Park seawall.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.text: Granville Island's market and makers, lunch by the water.

slots.label: Evening
slots.text: Dinner at Published on Main in Mount Pleasant, the city's tasting-menu leader.

slots.label: Morning
slots.text: A private drive up the Sea-to-Sky Highway to Squamish and the Sea to Sky Gondola.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.text: Whistler village or a return along Howe Sound with a stop at Britannia.

slots.label: Evening
slots.text: Dinner at Kissa Tanto in Chinatown for its Italian-Japanese kitchen.

slots.label: Morning
slots.text: The Museum of Anthropology at UBC for its Northwest Coast collection.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.text: The Capilano suspension bridge or a quieter walk at Lynn Canyon.

slots.label: Evening
slots.text: Omakase at Masayoshi in Kerrisdale to close the visit.

cta.label: Have your advisor arrange the stay

items.name: Coal Harbour
items.description: Glassy waterfront near Stanley Park and the seaplane terminal; the easy choice for a first stay.

items.name: Yaletown
items.description: Converted-warehouse blocks with the best restaurants and marina; suits those who want to walk to dinner.

items.name: Kitsilano
items.description: Beachy, low-rise and relaxed across the water; for travellers who want mornings by the sea, not the towers.

events.name: Vancouver International Wine Festival
events.note: The city's serious oenophile week, with a themed region and a large public tasting hall.

events.name: Vivid — Celebration of Light (fireworks)
events.note: Barge-launched international fireworks competition over English Bay across several nights.

events.name: Vancouver International Film Festival
events.note: One of North America's larger festivals, strong on Asian and Canadian cinema.

onGround.heading: On the ground

rows.label: Arriving
rows.value: Arrive into Vancouver International (YVR), about 30 minutes from downtown; a private car handles the transfer, or a floatplane can land you on the harbour beside Coal Harbour.

rows.label: Getting around
rows.value: A private driver suits the mountains-and-sea geography and day trips to Whistler; downtown, Stanley Park and Coal Harbour are pleasant on foot.

rows.label: Connectivity
rows.value: Canadian eSIMs activate instantly; wifi is fast throughout.

rows.label: Money
rows.value: Canadian dollars; cards and contactless everywhere; tip 18–20 percent in restaurants.

onGround.note: Stay in Coal Harbour or the West End for water and mountain views; it rains often outside summer, so waterproofs matter, and the drive to Whistler along the Sea-to-Sky highway is worth a full day.

rows.label: Climate
rows.value: July to September is dry, mild and luminous, with the mountains and sea at their best; November to February is grey and persistently wet — atmospheric, but not the trip to book for sun.

rows.label: Flights from India
rows.value: Air India flies Delhi to Vancouver direct, roughly 15-16 hours, comfortable in business; Air Canada also runs nonstop. Alternatively one stop via the Gulf (Emirates, Qatar) or a Pacific routing through Hong Kong (Cathay) — all strong up front, with fine lounges to break the journey.

rows.label: Health & safety
rows.value: No vaccinations required; tap water is pristine. Very safe; only routine caution, and note the visible tents and drug scene around parts of the Downtown Eastside, which is easily skirted. Rain, not risk, is the planning factor.

rows.label: Dining, veg & Jain
rows.value: Vegetarian and Jain needs are handled with ease across the city. A large South Asian community, especially in Surrey, means authentic and abundant Indian food — pure-veg thalis, chaat and South Indian are never far.

collections.lede: Every place we send you appears here on merit — follow the thread to more like it.
